<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 -->
# Independent hostile architecture validation, round 1

DISAGREE. Accuracy 91, completeness 89, confidence 98. Nine material implementer fixes; no operator decision FAIL. Claims: 8 PASS, 9 FAIL, 1 UNKNOWN (A4 renderer/page-level proof).

TimestampUtc: 2026-10-13T16:32:01.6875452Z. HEAD: bff6a7aadc2c138f89d99b8b77993cd603aa0d43. Reviewer: Codex, gpt-6-astra, effort max, thread 01a135e5-8784-77d0-a22d-9f6ef406b911. Live proof: /home/sharpninja/.codex/sessions/2026/10/13/rollout-2026-10-13T10-33-17-01a135e5-8784-77d0-a22d-9f6ef406b911.jsonl, turn_context 10/13/2026 15:33:21. The JSON receipt includes the complete turn_context record. No review time bound was applied.

Startup: add-profile skill and all 20 non-skill profile Markdown files read in full, including operator-rulings-2026-10-11.md; main workspace marker read in full; workflow.memory.list and all 15 memories read in full. MCP reviewer: Codex-20261013T153702Z-plugin-session / req-20261013T153316Z-hv-architecture-r1. Installed Codex wrapper with -ParamsObject, isolated cache outside worktree; no raw REST or Claude session-log wrapper.

The architecture is authoritative. The exact stateless copies pass. All 210 Mermaid blocks render; the recorded bounding boxes fit three full letter pages or fewer, but the complete renderer/page-level claim remains UNKNOWN. All 102 proposed requirement IDs are free. Publication ancestry and retained worktree pass. These successes do not resolve the functional defects below.

## Claims

- **R4: FAIL**. 13 of 14 R4 findings are resolved for their original counterexamples; R4-F8 is not. Earlier unresolved R3-F6 likewise remains. New dependency/projection failures are recorded separately.
  Findings: AR1-F6.

- **A1: FAIL**. Exact stateless copies pass for sections 3.5, 6, 7.11-7.16 and 8. Architecture authority fails on the derived-only alias contract.
  Findings: AR1-F1.

- **A2: FAIL**. The shared component organization is substantial, but shared alias access/delivery remains outside section 3.5.6 and defers its API to the plan.
  Findings: AR1-F1.

- **A3: PASS**. The declared RootNamespace+folder rule, separate request/handler files, one type per file and new PascalCase test names agree with the analyzer worktree. Storage RootNamespace is QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage there. Existing underscore names are historical source anchors, not new tests.

- **A4: UNKNOWN**. All 210 source blocks rendered twice with Mermaid 11.17.2/CLI 11.17.0, exit 0. At 8pt their bounding boxes fit at most three full letter pages, sequences landscape and others best orientation; three representative PNGs were inspected. The complete standard is not proven: the source has no renderer/pagination settings, and the independent render used ELK configuration plus Mermaid native sequences, which does not establish the literal dagre-for-sequences claim. The archived render recipe and actual page images must establish the requested renderer/font/routing standard; do not infer that proof from parse success or bounding boxes. Behavioral contradictions are scored under M3/M4.

- **A5: FAIL**. Live requirement snapshots and the catalog show extensive named reconciliation/test churn. The tool-audit loss is not an approved host limitation, and the turn-level decision contradicts the shared transaction contract.
  Findings: AR1-F4, AR1-F9.

- **A6: PASS**. The eleven catalog domains have bounded-context ownership, records, updated records, AC ownership, mappings and test churn. Domain work follows the section 8.3 context TODOs; coordinator decisions appear in the derived organization. The 102 proposed record count reconciles.

- **M1: FAIL**. All attached-plan topics are represented; Off/Pilot/Stateless, fail-invocation, HV turn ranges, default sources and token estimation are stated choices. Trust-chain and binding defects prevent the promised trustworthy package/response behavior.
  Findings: AR1-F2, AR1-F3.

- **M2: FAIL**. The entity/DTO/options/endpoint catalog is broad and includes REST aliases, MCP/client/REPL/PowerShell surfaces and errors. The alias public contract is absent from the authority, and model-grade verdict/runtime evidence acceptance is incomplete.
  Findings: AR1-F1, AR1-F8.

- **M3: FAIL**. CQRS units, policies, processes, activities, sequences, use cases and entity diagrams are indexed. Some sequences and nested activity lead-ins prescribe different behavior from their units/policies.
  Findings: AR1-F5, AR1-F6.

- **M4: FAIL**. Verified live REST/MCP shape distinctions, lifecycle payload whitelist, and terminal-submit guard at develop a8d3934b. Most R4 fidelity fixes hold, but the PowerShell port loses existing audit behavior and conflicting completion/recovery branches remain.
  Findings: AR1-F4, AR1-F5, AR1-F6.

- **M5: FAIL**. Concrete counterexamples break dependency freshness, whole-turn identity, projection cleanup, grade verification, and transaction scope. Cited live database uniqueness, GraphRAG allocation and dispatcher/workspace source anchors were checked.
  Findings: AR1-F2, AR1-F3, AR1-F7, AR1-F8, AR1-F9.

- **M6: PASS**. Four phases cover requirements, whole-plan seams/stubs, mock TDD, then owned contexts. The declared dependency and merge order is acyclic; context TODOs and gates are named. NOT APPROVED and the freeze remain explicit with only the operator-authorized analyzer exception.

- **M7: PASS**. Sections 8.4-8.5 and plan process rules use native Nuke builds/tests, direct infrastructure-only Build.Tests, Octopus for releases only, and Windows WSMan worktrees under F:/GitHub/McpServer/.worktrees. GitHub Actions/Azure Pipelines are not forward gates; historical/product mentions are distinguished.

- **M8: PASS**. Remote develop is a8d3934bc6238dc8e27f71c1d0561b55f48e88d4. Five named commits are consecutive parent-child, single-file publications; local remote reflog records each as update by push with no ancestry rewrite. Retained worktree/branch exist. Branch document blob ae14d3d1fc3afffa38fce8bb35ae3f17909d9dc0 differs from published 5f3ed62630d4c8a6594fd34a151cfb72c8efe51d. No push performed in this review.

- **M9: PASS**. Read-only main-workspace snapshots contain 353 FR, 487 TR and 512 TEST records. All 30 FR/39 TR/33 TEST proposed IDs are free. Owner/contributor rules and domain ownership lists resolve duplicate ownership; the specific changed-AC holes of R4-F12 now name owning TEST statements and cases. Phase C full AC text remains the explicitly authorized P0 catalog task.

- **M10: PASS**. All three documents have Apache-2.0 SPDX headers and zero en/em dash characters. Diff check passes; key-assignment scan reports zero in the reviewed documents and commit diff. Reviewer receipt exposure was separately corrected, not attributed to the reviewed artifacts.

- **M11: PASS**. lib-ps is the one designed core; existing Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 and plugin-hook.ps1 are real entry points with explicit planned additions. Host adapters contain only the permitted bindings. Pester/Nuke gates, retirement ordering and cross-agent ACK condition are named. Forward HV rules specify gpt-6-astra/max with no review time bound. The behavioral loss is separately a FAIL under M4/A5.

## Findings

### AR1-F1: The alias API is still designed only in the derived plan

Location: docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:251; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:483; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:547; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:1143; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:1234; docs/plans/PLAN-SESSIONTURN-SESSIONREVIEW-001.md:811.

C2 defers its interface to TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-008 AC-007. Only the plan defines four public PowerShell alias functions and the consumer-delivery data model. The architecture has no shared alias-access component in section 3.5.6 with those contracts and its test seam.

- Architecture line 251 says the interface is locked in TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-008 AC-007. The architecture contains no Register-McpAliasConsumer, Get-McpUnacknowledgedAlias, Get-McpAlias, or Confirm-McpAliasAcknowledged definition.

- Plan line 811 defines all four signatures, null/ambiguous lookup outcomes, permanent lookup entries, prunable delivery entries, and the consumer set captured at alias commit. Live writes and replay both consume the alias journal, so this is shared behavior, not merely a catalog label.

Change required: Move the complete alias model and four function contracts, error/return behavior, immutable host binding, atomicity and replay rules into one section 3.5.6 component owned by PluginCorePowerShell with one named Pester test seam. Make every alias caller reference it and derive AC-007 from it. No public contract may remain defined only in the plan.

Classification: Implementer edit. Operator decision: none. Architecture restructuring left an explicit design dependency on the plan.

### AR1-F2: A trusted response can depend on a response that is no longer trusted

Location: docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:457; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:463; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:2719; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:3047; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:3440; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:5972.

IResponseStalenessRule compares dependency hashes but never evaluates the effective trust/status of a PriorResponse dependency. PriorResponse and Package hashes are immutable content hashes. Dependency rejection, supersession, demotion, or staleness therefore does not invalidate descendants.

- Counterexample: trusted B is included in the package that produces trusted A. Reject B, or change a file that B depends on. B becomes Rejected or effectively Stale, but its ContentSha256 and the package ContentSha256 do not change. Every hash tested for A still matches; lines 464-465 return Fresh and A remains eligible for trusted retrieval.

- The rule explicitly special-cases deleted/superseded requirements, but has no corresponding prior-response status or recursive dependency check. Read-time freshness added for R4-F5 fixes direct changed-file reads but not this chain.

Change required: Extend the one shared staleness rule to validate effective trust and freshness of PriorResponse dependencies, including dependencies reached through packages. Define cycle handling and per-read memoization. Cover B becoming stale, rejected, superseded, or demoted while A content is unchanged; queries must exclude A immediately and EvaluateStaleness must persist the dependent invalidation.

Classification: Implementer edit. Operator decision: none. The R4 direct-read fix is present; its shared rule still admits an invalid trusted dependency chain.

### AR1-F3: Package recovery and supersession discard part of the turn key

Location: docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:175; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:2682; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:2683; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:3158; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:3159; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:3486; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:3803; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:3806; src/QBrainAi.Storage/McpDbContext.cs:391 at a8d3934b; src/QBrainAi.Storage/McpDbContext.cs:404 at a8d3934b.

The architecture declares the turn identity to be Agent + SessionId + RequestId, but recovery queries only requestId, invocation idempotency uses only requestId, and the supersede guard compares only requestId. Legacy turns with the same requestId in different sessions remain legal.

- The live database has a unique session key (WorkspaceId, SourceType, SessionId) and a unique turn key (SessionLogId, RequestId). The new workspace-wide minted-id index explicitly excludes legacy rows (Addendum A.2).

- Two legal turns with the same requestId can have distinct Built packages through the public build API. The fallback at line 3806 selects the newest package by requestId without the bound session/agent. Supersede at line 3486 likewise accepts a replacement belonging to the other turn. A workspace-wide idempotency key of requestId also collides for such roots.

Change required: Carry and check the full immutable turn key at recovery, submission binding, and supersession. Add an agent filter to package queries, require all three root fields when recovering the bound package, and derive a bounded deterministic invocation idempotency key from the full root. Test same requestId in two legacy sessions and two agents, including wrong-package recovery and cross-turn supersession refusal.

Classification: Implementer edit. Operator decision: none. The new root-id reconciliation is correct in the entities but incomplete at operational uses.

### AR1-F4: The PowerShell port removes working tool-audit behavior

Location: docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:137; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:243; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:255; docs/plans/PLAN-SESSIONTURN-SESSIONREVIEW-001.md:811; /home/sharpninja/github/mcpserver-cline-v2-plugin/src/plugin.ts:250; /home/sharpninja/github/mcpserver-opencode-plugin/src/plugin.ts:226; PLAN-SESSIONTURNREVIEW-001: approved description, C6.

The host-limit row drops beforeTool/afterTool and tool.execute.before/after solely because the PowerShell core has no audit hook. That is an unimplemented port, not a host infrastructure limitation. It contradicts C6 and removes behavior the approved Phase A contract preserved.

- At cline-v2 e776d942, lines 250-275 call core.appendToolAction before and after a tool. At opencode 36ed34d9, lines 226-254 do the same. The approved live TODO description and current architecture C6 require tool runs as tool_call/tool_result dialog items; QB-AGENT-001 owns the later tool_execution taxonomy, not permission to discard these existing records.

- The adapter allowlist excludes these hooks. The architecture lists the removal as a limitation but supplies neither an operator decision allowing it nor a replacement audit path and its parity tests.

Change required: Port the shared existing tool-audit behavior into the PowerShell core, define its hook input/output and error contract once, forward all four native hooks through the logic-free adapters, and preserve the tool_call/tool_result records under the bound turn identity. Carry the affected host/core tests and requirement reconciliation in that same change before retiring the Node path.

Classification: Implementer edit. Operator decision: none. PowerShell convergence currently deletes supported behavior; the operator authorized a port, not this deletion.

### AR1-F5: The replace sequence permits a completion-gate bypass

Location: docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:1466; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:1732; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:1734; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:2314; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:2323.

CompletionGate correctly applies to every Replace carrying completed or failed, including an already-terminal turn. The common sequence rule and Replace sequence narrow it to a status transition and recommend replacing without moving to a terminal status.

- A PUT of an already completed turn that omits its reviews is a replacement, not an additive enrichment. Lines 2314 and 2323 require re-gating it. Lines 1466 and 1732 do not, so following that sequence resets required review evidence while preserving completed.

- This is a conflicting executable branch, not a wording preference: the two definitions yield different responses to the same request.

Change required: Use the exact CompletionGate predicate in the common sequence rule and Replace sequence: a transition into completed/failed OR a Replace carrying either status. Show an already-completed replacement missing reviews returning the gate refusal. Keep additive terminal enrichment exempt. Add the corresponding negative case to the owning TEST statement.

Classification: Implementer edit. Operator decision: none. A holistic Phase B diagram inconsistency remains after the round-4 surface corrections.

### AR1-F6: First-ingress and mint-recovery instructions still contradict each other

Location: docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:991; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:992; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:1015; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:1026; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:1345; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:1873.

The nested mint activity says every answered mint clears the write-ahead record, while the authoritative retry rule retains final refusals with drainAttempts=1. The open-session sequence records mcpSessionId only after confirmed open, while first-ingress and SessionStart persist it before calling open so an outage cannot change the binding.

- For a final validation_error answer, line 991 keeps the record for bounded replay/quarantine; line 1015 clears it. This is the same final-refusal recovery defect R4-F8 required removing.

- For the first open timing out, lines 992/1026 retain the chosen MCP session identity, but line 1873 does not record it. Retrying under a newly generated identity can split the host session and strand its bound records.

Change required: Make all activities, lead-ins, and sequences use the shared classification and one lifecycle rule: success/merged-terminal/equal-field fail-close clear as specified; outage retains; final refusal retains and counts the first attempt. Persist the selected MCP session identity before the first open and reuse it after every outage. Add exact first-ingress outage and final-refusal readback cases.

Classification: Implementer edit. Operator decision: none. R4-F8 and its inherited R3-F6 remain NOT RESOLVED despite correct branches elsewhere.

### AR1-F7: Overlapping projection passes can orphan GraphRAG documents

Location: docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:2819; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:2821; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:3657; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:3658; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:4761; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:4764; src/QBrainAi.GraphRag/Services/GraphRagService.cs:354 at a8d3934b.

The deduplication rule preserves an overlapping document only when the row is Projected. A rejection during two concurrent ingests makes both saves Pending and lets the second overwrite the only stored document id. A post-ingest save exhaustion or failed duplicate cleanup also has no durable cleanup record.

- Concrete interleaving: passes P1/P2 both read Trusted with no projection and ingest D1/D2; Reject commits; P1 stores Pending+D1; P2 sees Pending, not Projected, and stores Pending+D2. The next pass deletes D2 and loses every reference to D1.

- The cited live IngestTextAsync allocates adhoc-<new Guid> on every call. The single GraphRagDocumentId column cannot retain both pending cleanup obligations. The four-attempt 409 path after external ingest similarly exits without defining how the new document is recovered.

Change required: Define durable per-response projection ownership or an outbox/operation record before ingest, with idempotent completion and a durable set of documents awaiting deletion. Preserve cleanup obligations in every row state and after failed saves/deletes. Test two ingests plus rejection, save exhaustion after ingest, and duplicate-delete failure; later passes must remove every untrusted/orphan document.

Classification: Implementer edit. Operator decision: none. The overlapping-Projected fix handles the happy interleaving but loses the reject/cleanup interleavings.

### AR1-F8: The model-grade acceptance checks do not fully establish the claimed evidence

Location: docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:2808; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:2811; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:2813; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:3718.

runtime_identity requires every turn_context to match but requires no turn_context to exist. A rollout containing only the matching session_meta passes that predicate without proving model or effort. Separately, verdict_match compares scores/findings but defines no verdict consistency rule for its required DISAGREE-with-passing-scores negative case.

- An empty set satisfies the universal test at line 2811. Matching request_meta, thread.started and session_meta identifiers are declarations/bindings, not the required live model/effort evidence.

- Line 2813 requires ModelGradeDisagreeVerdictPassingScoresRefusedVerdictMatch, but neither check 5 nor the per-response grades schema at line 3718 contains the predicate or per-entry verdict semantics needed to produce that refusal. This is especially ambiguous for a range with mixed passing and failing responses.

Change required: Require at least one review-run turn_context and bind its model/effort and thread to the completed review being graded; refuse missing runtime context explicitly. Define per-response verdict semantics and the batch overall verdict, validate their consistency with scores/findings, and make the named negative test match that rule without preventing legitimate failing grades or mixed ranges from being recorded.

Classification: Implementer edit. Operator decision: none. Live identity comparison is present, but missing evidence can still pass; the required verdict negative case has no defined acceptance rule.

### AR1-F9: Single-turn transaction scope still includes a shared session write

Location: docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:152; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:292; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:332; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:2125.

The locked turn-level decision isolates the turn and moves the session summary to a separate post-commit write. The shared SerializableWrite definition and Phase B write contract still read and write the common session row inside every single-turn transaction while promising different turns never conflict.

- Two different turns in one session address the same session row under the stated Serializable delegate. Concurrent updates to that shared row require serialization and can consume the same bounded transient-conflict retries the architecture exposes as 409.

- Line 152 explicitly makes summary refresh a separate write whose failure cannot fail the turn. Lines 332 and 2125 do not identify any other permitted session-row mutation or reconcile their in-transaction write with that decision.

Change required: Make the one shared transaction contract match the locked decision: locate/validate the parent as needed, but mutate only the target turn and its children inside a single-turn transaction; specify the session summary update as a separate post-commit operation with its own non-failing outcome. Define the provider-specific locking/read strategy and test concurrent writes to different turns plus a failed summary refresh.

Classification: Implementer edit. Operator decision: none. The round-5 turn-level reconciliation was not propagated consistently into the shared component and review units.

### AR1-F9: Single-turn transaction scope still includes a shared session write

Location: docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:152; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:292; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:332; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:2125.

The locked turn-level decision isolates the turn and moves the session summary to a separate post-commit write. The shared SerializableWrite definition and Phase B write contract still read and write the common session row inside every single-turn transaction while promising different turns never conflict.

- Two different turns in one session address the same session row under the stated Serializable delegate. Concurrent updates to that shared row require serialization and can consume the same bounded transient-conflict retries the architecture exposes as 409.

- Line 152 explicitly makes summary refresh a separate write whose failure cannot fail the turn. Lines 332 and 2125 do not identify any other permitted session-row mutation or reconcile their in-transaction write with that decision.

Change required: Make the one shared transaction contract match the locked decision: locate/validate the parent as needed, but mutate only the target turn and its children inside a single-turn transaction; specify the session summary update as a separate post-commit operation with its own non-failing outcome. Define the provider-specific locking/read strategy and test concurrent writes to different turns plus a failed summary refresh.

Classification: Implementer edit. Operator decision: none. The round-5 turn-level reconciliation was not propagated consistently into the shared component and review units.

Location: docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:457; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:463; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:2719; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:3047; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:3440; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:5972.

IResponseStalenessRule compares dependency hashes but never evaluates the effective trust/status of a PriorResponse dependency. PriorResponse and Package hashes are immutable content hashes. Dependency rejection, supersession, demotion, or staleness therefore does not invalidate descendants.

- Counterexample: trusted B is included in the package that produces trusted A. Reject B, or change a file that B depends on. B becomes Rejected or effectively Stale, but its ContentSha256 and the package ContentSha256 do not change. Every hash tested for A still matches; lines 464-465 return Fresh and A remains eligible for trusted retrieval.

- The rule explicitly special-cases deleted/superseded requirements, but has no corresponding prior-response status or recursive dependency check. Read-time freshness added for R4-F5 fixes direct changed-file reads but not this chain.

Change required: Extend the one shared staleness rule to validate effective trust and freshness of PriorResponse dependencies, including dependencies reached through packages. Define cycle handling and per-read memoization. Cover B becoming stale, rejected, superseded, or demoted while A content is unchanged; queries must exclude A immediately and EvaluateStaleness must persist the dependent invalidation.

Classification: Implementer edit. Operator decision: none. The R4 direct-read fix is present; its shared rule still admits an invalid trusted dependency chain.

### AR1-F3: Package recovery and supersession discard part of the turn key

- Two legal turns with the same requestId can have distinct Built packages through the public build API. The fallback at line 3806 selects the newest package by requestId without the bound session/agent. Supersede at line 3486 likewise accepts a replacement belonging to the other turn. A workspace-wide idempotency key of requestId also collides for such roots.

Add an agent filter to package queries, require all three root fields when recovering the bound package, and derive a bounded deterministic invocation idempotency key from the full root. Test same requestId in two legacy sessions and two agents, including wrong-package recovery and cross-turn supersession refusal.

runtime_identity requires every turn_context to match but requires no turn_context to exist. A rollout containing only the matching session_meta passes that predicate without proving model or effort. Separately, verdict_match compares scores/findings but defines no verdict consistency rule for its required DISAGREE-with-passing-scores negative case.

- An empty set satisfies the universal test at line 2811. Matching request_meta, thread.started and session_meta identifiers are declarations/bindings, not the required live model/effort evidence.

- Line 2813 requires ModelGradeDisagreeVerdictPassingScoresRefusedVerdictMatch, but neither check 5 nor the per-response grades schema at line 3718 contains the predicate or per-entry verdict semantics needed to produce that refusal. This is especially ambiguous for a range with mixed passing and failing responses.

Change required: Require at least one review-run turn_context and bind its model/effort and thread to the completed review being graded; refuse missing runtime context explicitly. Define per-response verdict semantics and the batch overall verdict, validate their consistency with scores/findings, and make the named negative test match that rule without preventing legitimate failing grades or mixed ranges from being recorded.

### AR1-F9: Single-turn transaction scope still includes a shared session write

Location: docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:152; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:292; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:332; docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:2125.

The locked turn-level decision isolates the turn and moves the session summary to a separate post-commit write. The shared SerializableWrite definition and Phase B write contract still read and write the common session row inside every single-turn transaction while promising different turns never conflict.

- Two different turns in one session address the same session row under the stated Serializable delegate. Concurrent updates to that shared row require serialization and can consume the same bounded transient-conflict retries the architecture exposes as 409.

- Line 152 explicitly makes summary refresh a separate write whose failure cannot fail the turn. Lines 332 and 2125 do not identify any other permitted session-row mutation or reconcile their in-transaction write with that decision.

Change required: Make the one shared transaction contract match the locked decision: locate/validate the parent as needed, but mutate only the target turn and its children inside a single-turn transaction; specify the session summary update as a separate post-commit operation with its own non-failing outcome. Define the provider-specific locking/read strategy and test concurrent writes to different turns plus a failed summary refresh.

Classification: Implementer edit. Operator decision: none. The round-5 turn-level reconciliation was not propagated consistently into the shared component and review units.

8: How to read the diagrams:
9: 
10: - Activity diagrams are Mermaid flowcharts read top to bottom. A rounded terminal is a start or an end, a diamond is a decision, a rectangle is an action, and every error exit is drawn and ends in a terminal that names the error code.
11: - Sequence diagrams show who sends what. Each `alt` block lists every response the caller can receive and how the caller processes it.
12: - Three kinds of activity diagram: a unit of work is exactly one CQRS command or query with its handler (operator, 2026-10-11: "I want to be clear, unit of work maps to one CQRS handler") and is labelled by the record's name; a policy is a rule a handler applies (for example CompletionGate); a process is plugin, host, REPL, or build orchestration that calls handlers (for example ApplyArrivalBridgeRecord). All labels are meaningful names (operator: "Please use human-readable, meaningful identifiers."). Section 3.5 also draws each shared component once, as the activity diagram of that component.
13: - A double-bordered node (`[["..."]]`) is a call: a shared component of section 3.5, a policy, or a process used as a step. The calling diagram draws only the exits the call returns, labelled by its typed results; the called steps are drawn once, where the callee is defined.
14: - Requirement ids in brackets name the functional requirement the unit of work realizes. Ids of the form `FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-*` are reserved for Phase 1 (the plan's P0 steps 1-9), where the agent-context catalog is created.
15: 
16: ## 1. Goals
17: 
18: 1. One user request is exactly one session-log turn, minted by the server when the message arrives, and every write lands on the turn of the request that caused it (Phase A).
19: 2. Every turn carries a request class and two review records (agent and hostile) with lossless decimal scores, a status lifecycle, configurable thresholds, and a server-enforced completion gate (Phase B).
20: 3. Every agent invocation can run stateless: the server builds a bounded, reproducible context package from the profile, rules, requirements, session-log evidence, trusted prior responses, and current code, and only responses graded at 98/98 with no FAIL or UNKNOWN become trusted context for later requests (Phase C).
21: 
22: The agent-context scope depends on the turn-logging scope (turns are the unit a package is built for, and session-log turns are evidence) and on the review scope (the thresholds and the 98/98 grading rule). Logic that more than one unit of work, policy, or process uses is one shared component (section 3.5), defined once and called from each user (operator, 2026-10-12: "If a pice of logic is hared between multiple UoW, that logic should be encapsulated and shared."). Phases A, B, and C name scope areas; execution runs in four phases across all three (section 8): requirements, interfaces and code stubs, test-driven unit tests with mocks, and implementation by bounded context with parallel coding agents.

77: ## 3. Cross-cutting conventions, design decisions, and contracts
78: 
79: - Workspace scoping: every request is scoped to one workspace through the `X-Workspace-Path` header (REST), the `workspacePath` parameter (MCP tools, REPL), or `MCP_WORKSPACE_PATH` (plugins); WorkspaceResolutionBehavior (section 3.5.1) resolves it for every command and query, existing ones included, into the `WorkspaceContext` of the caller's dispatch scope (`IDispatcher` becomes scoped), and a record that may run with no workspace (global memory) declares `IAllowsGlobalWorkspace`. Every stored record carries its `WorkspaceId`, and no read ever crosses workspaces.
80: - Authentication: `X-Api-Key` (or `api_key`) from the workspace marker. Plugins never call REST directly; they use the REPL wrapper.
81: - Plugin scripting: PowerShell only (operator, 2026-10-11: "You should be designing all scripts and script tools around PowerShell and only PowerShell."). `plugins/core/lib-ps` is the one plugin core for all nine hosts; cline, cline-v2, and opencode keep only the adapter entry file their host API forces, which forwards each host hook invocation the host binding table names (`{ input, output }`; on opencode's `event` hook, which fires for every host event including streaming updates, only an event of type `session.idle`, so no other event starts `pwsh`) to `lib/plugin-hook.ps1 -HostEvent` and applies the returned `output`, forwards each tool call (`{ params, hostContext }`) to `lib/Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 -InvocationFromStdin`, and registers the tools listed in `lib/tool-descriptors.json`; the host's own build compiles that one file into the git-ignored `dist/`; Pester is the only plugin test runner.
82: - Routes: every REST route exists under `/qbrainai/...` with the legacy alias `/mcpserver/...`.
83: - Errors: every REST error of a unit this plan adds or changes is the `ClassifiedError` problem+json body `{ "type", "title", "status", "detail", "code", "message", "retryable", "details" }` emitted through `McpErrorClassifier` (`SessionLogController.cs` and the agent-context controller) from the handler's `ClassifiedErrorException` (section 3.5.2); `code` carries the unit's error code (for example `review_status_conflict`, `agent_context_budget_exceeded`), the HTTP status is the one stated per unit (400 validation, 403 not allowed, 404 not found, 409 conflict or disabled, 422 semantic refusal), and MCP tools return `{ code, error, message, retryable, details }`. A 409 `conflict` carries `retryable: true` when SerializableWrite or key allocation exhausted its retries (four attempts; only the Phase A minter states its own bound, for a collision of its random request id only, six attempts and 500 `mint_collision_exhausted`, while its transient conflicts keep the four attempts and the 409, section 3.5.2), which is also the answer when a deadlock or a busy store outlasts those attempts, and `retryable: false` when an idempotency key is reused with other inputs; the plugin treats a retryable 409 as an outage and keeps its failsafe record (a review excepted: reviews keep their no-failsafe rule, section 3.1); a busy store outside SerializableWrite keeps today's 503 `persistence_error` with `retryable: true` (`src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/Services/McpErrorClassifier.cs:129-139` at `a8d3934b`), and unreachable storage keeps its answer (section 3.1, "Deadlock and busy outcomes"). A workspace that does not resolve is 400 `validation_error` with `details.field` `workspacePath` on every surface, the status TR-MCP-MT-002 gives an unregistered workspace (WorkspaceResolutionBehavior, section 3.5.1), and every sequence draws that refusal after the dispatch. On REST, `WorkspaceResolutionMiddleware` still answers a missing or unknown `X-Workspace-Path` before any controller with today's `{ error }` bodies (400 for an unknown path and 404 for a workspace-required route with none, `src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/Middleware/WorkspaceResolutionMiddleware.cs:106-111,171-177` at `a8d3934b`). Those middleware bodies, and every existing body a unit keeps as today (stated per unit, for example the dialog route's `{ error }` 400 and the "Invalid turn body." problem), are outside this plan's error rule: they stay as they are on develop, and FR-MCP-TRIAGEERR-001's acceptance criterion of a machine-readable envelope on every REST failure is recorded as deliberately left open for them, as it is on develop. On success, `sessionlog_record_review` returns `{ success: true, review }` with the review record (`SessionLogTurnReviewDto`), each `agent_context_*` tool returns its unit's result DTO as camelCase JSON, and every existing tool keeps its shape (sections 4.2 and 5.2); MCP carries no HTTP status, so a status a diagram shows is the REST status, and an MCP caller tells a created record from an existing one only where the result says so (`created` on a relationship). The completion gate is the one exception to the code rule: its `code` is `validation_error` and its message starts with the token `session_turn_completion_gate` followed by the missing items in the order requestClass, agentReview, hostileReview (FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002-AC006); the diagrams name that refusal by its token. Existing routes whose behavior this plan does not change keep today's error bodies (for example the `{ error }` 400 of the dialog route and the "Invalid session identifier." problem of the open and title routes), stated per unit, and a body-binding failure keeps today's validation problem with `errors` keyed by JSON path (section 3.4, Errors, which reconciles FR-SUPPORT-012). The REPL error envelope is `type: error` with `code`, `message`, and `retryable`.
84: - Identifiers: every identifier is human-readable and meaningful (operator, 2026-10-11: "Please use human-readable, meaningful identifiers."). Session ids `<Agent>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<suffix>`; server-minted request ids `req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<8 hex>`; agent-context record keys derive from the turn and session they belong to (section 6.3): packages `pkg-<requestId>-<nn>`, responses `rsp-<requestId>-<nn>`, grades `grd-<responseId>-<kind>-<nn>`, relationships `rel-<type>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<nn>`, HV requests `hvr-<sessionId>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>`; ReadableKeyAllocator (section 3.5.2) allocates every one of these keys and the server-minted request ids. Document labels use the command, query, process, policy, and shared component names. Namespaces say where a type goes and who owns it, and type and member names say what it is and what it does (section 3.5).
85: - Root ids: every record carries `WorkspaceId` and the root ids of every parent it hangs from, a turn's root id being its whole turn key (`Agent`, `SessionId`, `RequestId`): a turn child the turn key; a package child `PackageId` and the turn key; a response child `ResponseId`, `PackageId`, and the turn key; a grade those and, for a model grade, `HvRequestId`; an HV request item `HvRequestId`, `ResponseId`, `PackageId`, and the turn key (section 3.1, "Root ids"; section 6.3).
86: - Changes to existing behavior: no phase is purely additive. Phase C adds tables, endpoints, and the `Mcp:AgentContext:Mode` setting, but the shared components it brings change behavior every existing caller sees, in every Mode: `IDispatcher` in the published `QBrainAI.Cqrs` package becomes scoped and WorkspaceResolutionBehavior runs on every command and query (section 3.5.1); a deadlock or busy store that outlasts SerializableWrite's attempts answers 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` where develop answers 503 (section 3.5.2); the published `QBrainAI.Client` package gains the new DTOs, `ClassifiedErrorException`, `ErrorCodes`, `PageResult`, and `ScoreLexeme` (section 8.1, "Published packages", states each package's version effect: the client additions a minor version, the scoped `IDispatcher` a major version under semantic versioning). Phases A and B change turn identity (server-minted request ids), turn writes (turn-level isolation, `closed` refused on agent surfaces, the completion gate), and the plugin's per-turn store; the TypeScript hosts' tool audit moves into the PowerShell core and keeps its `tool_call` and `tool_result` dialog items but writes no `design_decision` action per tool event (section 3.2, Tool-audit hook). Where this document states a behavior that replaces a live requirement record, it names the record inline once, in the form "(replaces ...)", so the plan lists every update.
87: - Secrets: no API key, token, password, or credential is ever stored in a context package or a response, and none is ever returned by a read surface; turn text is stored as written, searched as stored, and redacted on every read surface (FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGSAN-001, its ac4 for the search; section 3.4, Search); `SecretRedactor` (section 3.5.2) is the one redactor behind the session-log sanitizer's review paths, the turn read projection, and the agent-context secret filter and secret scan.
88: - Process: the plan runs in the four execution phases of section 8 under the Byrd Development Process v4 (requirements, tests red, mocks green, implementation green, full gates with zero failures and zero skips); each prerequisite, the end of Phase 1, Phase 2, and Phase 3, each bounded context at the end of its Phase 4 work package, and the phase-wide Phase 4 HV end with a Codex gpt-6-astra max hostile validation at accuracy and completeness of at least 98 with every claim PASS. Builds and tests run as Nuke targets natively on Windows or Linux; GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines are not part of any requirement or process; Octopus (container on LAB-OMARCHY) is used only for releases.

93: Locked operator decisions of 2026-10-09:
94: 
95: Turn logging
96: - Every user request (including messages queued mid-turn) is exactly one turn; actions and decisions map to the turn of the request that caused them, determined by the write-attribution rule below (D2). Enforcement of turn-logging correctness is Phase A and ships first.
97: - Plugin turn edits are independent: opening, editing, closing, or canceling one turn never changes another turn's local or server state; concurrent edits to different turns do not interfere.
98: - Unsupported-session failsafe (operator, 2026-10-10: "If QBrain is truly not available, use the failsafe already in the plugin." and, choosing between a failsafe capture and a warn-only Stop, "1"): when a host session fails closed under D6 (`unsupportedSince`), the model's session-log writes for a turn that was already open at that moment go to the plugin's existing failsafe instead of being refused (reviews excepted: they keep their no-failsafe rule and are recorded after the drain through the original pair), so the Stop gate's remedy stays accepted; the captured records drain at the next SessionStart through the trusted recovery flow with the turn's original pair (C5); every mint and every write for any other turn stays refused (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001).
99: - Clear-session closing rule (operator, 2026-10-10, choosing option A over leaving blocked and withdrawn turns open: "A"): clear-session completes each turn that meets the completion policy, fails each withdrawn turn (reason "withdrawn before delivery") and each turn the model marks blocked (with its blocker reason; `failed` requires `requestClass` only, FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002-AC002), and leaves every other turn in progress, reported by requestId with its exact missing items, never fabricating reviews (TR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001-AC001). Definition (catalog cross-reference, not a change to the decision): "marked blocked" means the turn's `blockers` section (the existing decision-list field, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-006-AC001) holds at least one nonblank model-authored entry, read by the clear-session coordinator for that turn by its original (`sessionId`, `requestId`) pair, and the first entry is the fail reason; precedence per turn: withdrawn -> `failTurn` ("withdrawn before delivery"); else blocked -> `failTurn` with the blocker reason (blocked takes precedence over a ready completion); else meets the completion policy -> `completeTurn`; else stays in progress, reported with its exact missing items. Close prerequisites (catalog cross-reference, not a change to the decision): before clear-session fails a withdrawn or blocked turn, the model writes by that turn's original pair, within the same clear-session run and before its session-end step, every prerequisite the plugin and the server require for that close, in the Stop gate remedy order (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC009): a designDecision when the turn has no model evidence (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC002), then a `requestClass` when it is missing or `Unclassified`, judged from the turn's `queryText`; the coordinator then fails the turn with its reason (TR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001-AC001).
100: - Request identity (operator D1, 2026-10-09: "have the server issue a request token when a message arrives"): the server mints every turn's `requestId` when a user message arrives (ingress), through the new mint operation `POST /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/mint`. The mint call carries an idempotency nonce derived from the host's own identity for that message event (host binding table, section 3.2): a host per-prompt id, or a SHA-256 of host event fields that every delivery of that event carries identically. Every delivery of one event therefore sends the same nonce and receives the same token, including network retries and failsafe replay on every host and, on hosts whose nonce is a stable per-message id (codex `turn_id`, grok and grok-bot `promptId`, cline-v2 `runId`, opencode `messageID`) or the bridge's single ordered source (claude-code, claude-cowork), two hook processes started by a doubly registered hook (on copilot and classic cline a second registration is refused before any mint, and a second new equal-field invocation fails closed); two separate user messages (including two intentionally identical prompts) are two events and receive two tokens. On copilot and classic cline, whose event fields include no per-message id, a message whose session, timestamp, and prompt all equal an already minted one is indistinguishable from a redelivery of it, so the host session fails closed under D6 instead of merging or guessing (host binding table, equal-field rule). The host id is only the idempotency key; the turn identity is the server-issued token. There is no prompt-text dedupe window. Every mint comes from a host arrival mechanism (a prompt hook, the arrival bridge, or a host-native hook adapter); no supported host relies on the model to mint. The stop gate's `duplicate_delivery_suspected` warning is a diagnostic only and is never counted as D1 compliance.
101: - Queued-message arrival (operator D5, 2026-10-09: "Arrival bridge"): a message the operator sends while a turn is running is minted when it is enqueued, not when the model later processes it. On hosts that record the enqueue in a transcript (Claude Code), a per-host-session arrival bridge started by the SessionStart hook tails the transcript and follows each queued message through the lifecycle the transcript records. Observed in this workspace's Claude Code transcripts on 2026-10-09: 117 `enqueue`, 79 `dequeue`, 35 `remove` (27 with reason `absorbed_mid_turn`), 2 `popAll`; a normal prompt is `enqueue` then `dequeue` within milliseconds, a mid-turn message is `enqueue` then `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn` when it is injected into the running turn (for example the operator's mid-turn message beginning "write a global memory with the" was removed with `absorbed_mid_turn` at 2026-10-09T14:35:47.730Z), and `popAll` pulls queued text back into the input box. The bridge mints at `enqueue` (state `queued`); the request becomes `delivered` at `dequeue` (applied by the bridge from the transcript itself; on hosts with a bridge the prompt hook neither mints nor claims) or at `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn`; it becomes `withdrawn` at `popAll` or a `remove` with any other or no reason. Task notifications and other system events that the host also enqueues are classified and never minted; on bridge hosts they keep their queue position (`kind: system`), so their `dequeue` never delivers a user request.
102: - Hosts without an arrival mechanism (operator D6, 2026-10-09: "Adapters or unsupported"): a host is supported for turn logging only through an arrival mechanism this plan specifies (a prompt hook that fires at enqueue, the claude-code/claude-cowork arrival bridge, or the classic-cline native-hook adapter); every other host is unsupported until a separately approved adapter exists, and a queue or enqueue event that P0.2 records on such a host becomes a traced follow-up adapter TODO (filed in P0.8) for operator approval (host binding table, section 3.2). A host with no arrival mechanism is declared unsupported for turn logging until it gains one: its plugin reports `turn_logging_unsupported` on every session-log verb and writes nothing (a host session that becomes unsupported after one of its requests was delivered follows the host binding table unsupported-session rule and the 2026-10-10 failsafe decision), and no first-sight minting is used anywhere.
103: - Plugin equivalence (operator D7, 2026-10-09, confirmed in chat "1 yes" for the requirement and its qualification posted by Codex in `MEMORY-PROCESS-007` at 17:48:48Z and 17:52:06Z): all QBrain.AI plugins keep equivalent functionality; shared capabilities, contracts, fixes, and behavior changes go to every plugin; host-specific adaptations preserve equivalent supported behavior; equivalence is limited by what each host's plugin infrastructure can support, no extraordinary effort is spent forcing unworkable equivalence, and each such limit is documented as a feature-specific capability limitation instead of being claimed as equivalent. A D6 `turn_logging_unsupported` host is such a documented limitation. The limitations live in `docs/AGENT-PLUGIN-FEATURE-MATRIX.md` (one row per plugin and feature: supported, adapted, or limited, with the reason and the receipt), first written in P0.8 from the P0.2 receipts, updated in A9 and S11, and checked by a docs contract test.
104: - Ninth plugin (operator D8, 2026-10-09: "2 yes"): `mcpserver-grok-bot-plugin` is in scope like the other eight.
105: - Write attribution (operator D2, 2026-10-09: tie each write to its request automatically through the agent app's hooks): every verb invocation is bound to one request automatically from host context, without the model naming it: the binding is the write target of the invoking host session at the moment the invocation starts, captured once and stored immutably with that invocation (its persist record and failsafe record), so a later message never retargets an invocation already started. A host session's write target is the request most recently delivered to the model in that host session: a prompt the host hands to the model as a new turn (the prompt hook on hosts without a bridge, or the bridge's `dequeue` delivery), or a queued message absorbed into the running turn (`absorbed_mid_turn`). Minting alone never moves the write target, so work the model is still doing for request R1 after R2 is enqueued stays on R1 until R2 is delivered. Explicit `requestId` remains accepted as an override, for example to continue R1 work after R2 was absorbed, and it is required while two or more delivered requests are open in the host session (D9). Attribution therefore maps each write to the request most recently delivered to the model in its host session when the write started. A write is never attributed by guesswork: when a verb cannot read its host session key from its own invocation context (host binding table, section 3.2), it binds only if exactly one live host session of its agent exists in the workspace (warning `host_session_inferred`); with none it is refused (`host_session_unknown`), and with more than one it is refused (`host_session_ambiguous`), in both cases unless it carries the trusted recovery or review-backfill pair (original MCP `sessionId` and `requestId`, verified against the server for this workspace and agent, C5); an explicit `requestId` alone never lets a verb without a host session key write. No verb ever targets the workspace-level `current-turn.yaml`.
106: - Ambiguous attribution (operator D9, 2026-10-09: "Refuse when ambiguous"): no host supplies a per-action signal of which request caused a write, so automatic binding applies only while exactly one delivered request is open in the host session. While two or more delivered requests are open (for example R2 absorbed mid-turn while R1 is still open), a write without an explicit `requestId` is refused with `request_ambiguous`, naming the open requests; the model passes `requestId` until all but one are closed. Writes are never attributed by guesswork.
107: - Copilot duplicate deliveries (operator D11, 2026-10-09: "Supported only if single hook"): Copilot gives no stable per-prompt id and separately registered hooks may see different `timestamp` values, so Copilot turn logging is supported only while the plugin's duplicate check proves exactly one MCP prompt hook across all Copilot hook sources; otherwise the Copilot prompt hook reports `turn_logging_unsupported` before any mint, and the condition is a D7 documented limitation until fixed. One Copilot prompt therefore never becomes two turns.

Exact review scores are validated and carried by the PowerShell core's raw-lexeme rules (S8); the adapters never parse a score (C10).

# Copilot Instructions — QBrainAi

**Agent Identity:** When posting to the MCP session log, use the agent's actual identity in Pascal-Case for `sourceType` and the session ID prefix. Do not use inaccurate aliases, lowercase names, or legacy placeholders. Example: `Codex`.
For specific operational instructions (session bootstrap, turn logging lifecycle, helper command order), follow `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`.

## Response Formatting

- Do not use table-style output in responses.
- Use concise bullets or short paragraphs instead.

## Terminal Usage

- Do NOT set focus to the terminal window.
- Do NOT write multiline commands to the terminal; use temporary scripts instead.
- Use **only `pwsh.exe`** (PowerShell 7+). Do not invoke `powershell.exe` (Windows PowerShell 5.1) for scripts, examples, or tooling.

## Session Logging Requirements

- Follow `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` for workflow and helper command order.
- Persist session log changes immediately after each meaningful update; do not batch unsaved turn changes.
- For each turn, include as much detail as available: interpretation, response/status, actions (type/status/filePath), files modified, design decisions, requirements discovered, blockers, and context references.

## Build, Test, Lint

```powershell
# Build (via Nuke)
./build.ps1 Compile
# or: dotnet build src\QBrainAi.Support.Mcp -c Debug

# Run all unit tests (via Nuke)
./build.ps1 Test
# or individual projects:
# dotnet test tests\QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Tests -c Debug
# dotnet test tests\QBrainAi.Client.Tests -c Debug
# dotnet test tests\Build.Tests -c Debug

# Run integration tests (uses CustomWebApplicationFactory, in-memory EF)
dotnet test tests\QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.IntegrationTests -c Debug

# Run a single test by fully-qualified name
dotnet test tests\QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Tests -c Debug --filter "FullyQualifiedName~TodoServiceTests.QueryAsync_NoFilters_ReturnsAllItems"

# Run tests in a single class
dotnet test tests\QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Tests -c Debug --filter "FullyQualifiedName~TodoServiceTests"

# Validate appsettings config (via Nuke)
./build.ps1 ValidateConfig
# or: pwsh.exe -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File ./scripts/Validate-McpConfig.ps1

# Validate requirements traceability
./build.ps1 ValidateTraceability

# Markdown lint (docs only)
# CI uses markdownlint-cli2 with .markdownlint-cli2.yaml
```

## Architecture

**QBrainAi** is a standalone ASP.NET Core 9 server providing context retrieval, TODO management, session logging, repository operations, and GitHub issue sync for AI agents. It exposes functionality via two transports:

- **HTTP REST API** — Controllers under `src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/Controllers/` (routes at `/qbrainai/*`).
- **MCP Streamable HTTP** — `app.MapMcp("/mcp-transport")` using ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore.
- **MCP STDIO** — `--transport stdio` flag; same tools as HTTP via `McpStdio/FwhMcpTools.cs`.

**Workspace model**: The primary host manages multiple workspaces, each getting its own in-process Kestrel `WebApplication` (not child processes). Workspace config lives in `appsettings.json` under `Mcp:Workspaces` (not in the database). One workspace is the "primary" — served by the host process directly; others get child `WebApplication` instances via `WorkspaceAppFactory`.

**Search pipeline**: Hybrid search combines SQLite FTS5 full-text with HNSW vector similarity (384-dim all-MiniLM-L6-v2 ONNX embeddings). `HybridSearchService` fuses both with BM25 scoring.

**Storage**: EF Core with SQLite (`McpDbContext`). TODO items use a pluggable backend — either YAML file-backed (`TodoService`) or SQLite table-backed (`SqliteTodoService`), selected via `Mcp:TodoStorage:Provider`.

**Multi-instance**: `McpInstanceResolver` overlays per-instance config from `Mcp:Instances:{name}` onto base `Mcp:*` settings.

## Key Conventions

### XML Documentation Required

`TreatWarningsAsErrors` and `GenerateDocumentationFile` are enabled globally in `Directory.Build.props`. All public types and members must have XML doc comments or the build fails (CS1591). Use `/// <inheritdoc />` for interface implementations. Test projects are not exempt: test classes and test methods must include XML docs that state what is being tested, what data/fixtures are used, why that data/fixtures are used, and which requirement IDs are validated.

### Requirement Traceability Comments

All source files reference their FR/TR requirement IDs in doc comments (e.g., `/// <summary>TR-PLANNED-CORE-013: Constructor.</summary>`). When adding new functionality, reference the relevant requirement ID from `docs/Project/Functional-Requirements.md` and `docs/Project/Technical-Requirements.md`.

95: Turn logging
96: - Every user request (including messages queued mid-turn) is exactly one turn; actions and decisions map to the turn of the request that caused them, determined by the write-attribution rule below (D2). Enforcement of turn-logging correctness is Phase A and ships first.
97: - Plugin turn edits are independent: opening, editing, closing, or canceling one turn never changes another turn's local or server state; concurrent edits to different turns do not interfere.
98: - Unsupported-session failsafe (operator, 2026-10-10: "If QBrain is truly not available, use the failsafe already in the plugin." and, choosing between a failsafe capture and a warn-only Stop, "1"): when a host session fails closed under D6 (`unsupportedSince`), the model's session-log writes for a turn that was already open at that moment go to the plugin's existing failsafe instead of being refused (reviews excepted: they keep their no-failsafe rule and are recorded after the drain through the original pair), so the Stop gate's remedy stays accepted; the captured records drain at the next SessionStart through the trusted recovery flow with the turn's original pair (C5); every mint and every write for any other turn stays refused (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001).
99: - Clear-session closing rule (operator, 2026-10-10, choosing option A over leaving blocked and withdrawn turns open: "A"): clear-session completes each turn that meets the completion policy, fails each withdrawn turn (reason "withdrawn before delivery") and each turn the model marks blocked (with its blocker reason; `failed` requires `requestClass` only, FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002-AC002), and leaves every other turn in progress, reported by requestId with its exact missing items, never fabricating reviews (TR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001-AC001). Definition (catalog cross-reference, not a change to the decision): "marked blocked" means the turn's `blockers` section (the existing decision-list field, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-006-AC001) holds at least one nonblank model-authored entry, read by the clear-session coordinator for that turn by its original (`sessionId`, `requestId`) pair, and the first entry is the fail reason; precedence per turn: withdrawn -> `failTurn` ("withdrawn before delivery"); else blocked -> `failTurn` with the blocker reason (blocked takes precedence over a ready completion); else meets the completion policy -> `completeTurn`; else stays in progress, reported with its exact missing items. Close prerequisites (catalog cross-reference, not a change to the decision): before clear-session fails a withdrawn or blocked turn, the model writes by that turn's original pair, within the same clear-session run and before its session-end step, every prerequisite the plugin and the server require for that close, in the Stop gate remedy order (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC009): a designDecision when the turn has no model evidence (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC002), then a `requestClass` when it is missing or `Unclassified`, judged from the turn's `queryText`; the coordinator then fails the turn with its reason (TR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001-AC001).
100: - Request identity (operator D1, 2026-10-09: "have the server issue a request token when a message arrives"): the server mints every turn's `requestId` when a user message arrives (ingress), through the new mint operation `POST /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/mint`. The mint call carries an idempotency nonce derived from the host's own identity for that message event (host binding table, section 3.2): a host per-prompt id, or a SHA-256 of host event fields that every delivery of that event carries identically. Every delivery of one event therefore sends the same nonce and receives the same token, including network retries and failsafe replay on every host and, on hosts whose nonce is a stable per-message id (codex `turn_id`, grok and grok-bot `promptId`, cline-v2 `runId`, opencode `messageID`) or the bridge's single ordered source (claude-code, claude-cowork), two hook processes started by a doubly registered hook (on copilot and classic cline a second registration is refused before any mint, and a second new equal-field invocation fails closed); two separate user messages (including two intentionally identical prompts) are two events and receive two tokens. On copilot and classic cline, whose event fields include no per-message id, a message whose session, timestamp, and prompt all equal an already minted one is indistinguishable from a redelivery of it, so the host session fails closed under D6 instead of merging or guessing (host binding table, equal-field rule). The host id is only the idempotency key; the turn identity is the server-issued token. There is no prompt-text dedupe window. Every mint comes from a host arrival mechanism (a prompt hook, the arrival bridge, or a host-native hook adapter); no supported host relies on the model to mint. The stop gate's `duplicate_delivery_suspected` warning is a diagnostic only and is never counted as D1 compliance.
101: - Queued-message arrival (operator D5, 2026-10-09: "Arrival bridge"): a message the operator sends while a turn is running is minted when it is enqueued, not when the model later processes it. On hosts that record the enqueue in a transcript (Claude Code), a per-host-session arrival bridge started by the SessionStart hook tails the transcript and follows each queued message through the lifecycle the transcript records. Observed in this workspace's Claude Code transcripts on 2026-10-09: 117 `enqueue`, 79 `dequeue`, 35 `remove` (27 with reason `absorbed_mid_turn`), 2 `popAll`; a normal prompt is `enqueue` then `dequeue` within milliseconds, a mid-turn message is `enqueue` then `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn` when it is injected into the running turn (for example the operator's mid-turn message beginning "write a global memory with the" was removed with `absorbed_mid_turn` at 2026-10-09T14:35:47.730Z), and `popAll` pulls queued text back into the input box. The bridge mints at `enqueue` (state `queued`); the request becomes `delivered` at `dequeue` (applied by the bridge from the transcript itself; on hosts with a bridge the prompt hook neither mints nor claims) or at `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn`; it becomes `withdrawn` at `popAll` or a `remove` with any other or no reason. Task notifications and other system events that the host also enqueues are classified and never minted; on bridge hosts they keep their queue position (`kind: system`), so their `dequeue` never delivers a user request.
102: - Hosts without an arrival mechanism (operator D6, 2026-10-09: "Adapters or unsupported"): a host is supported for turn logging only through an arrival mechanism this plan specifies (a prompt hook that fires at enqueue, the claude-code/claude-cowork arrival bridge, or the classic-cline native-hook adapter); every other host is unsupported until a separately approved adapter exists, and a queue or enqueue event that P0.2 records on such a host becomes a traced follow-up adapter TODO (filed in P0.8) for operator approval (host binding table, section 3.2). A D6 `turn_logging_unsupported` host is such a documented limitation. The limitations live in `docs/AGENT-PLUGIN-FEATURE-MATRIX.md` (one row per plugin and feature: supported, adapted, or limited, with the reason and the receipt), first written in P0.8 from the P0.2 receipts, updated in A9 and S11, and checked by a docs contract test.

105: - Write attribution (operator D2, 2026-10-09: tie each write to its request automatically through the agent app's hooks): every verb invocation is bound to one request automatically from host context, without the model naming it: the binding is the write target of the invoking host session at the moment the invocation starts, captured once and stored immutably with that invocation (its persist record and failsafe record), so a later message never retargets an invocation already started. A host session's write target is the request most recently delivered to the model in that host session: a prompt the host hands to the model as a new turn (the prompt hook on hosts without a bridge, or the bridge's `dequeue` delivery), or a queued message absorbed into the running turn (`absorbed_mid_turn`). Minting alone never moves the write target, so work the model is still doing for request R1 after R2 is enqueued stays on R1 until R2 is delivered. Explicit `requestId` remains accepted as an override, for example to continue R1 work after R2 was absorbed, and it is required while two or more delivered requests are open in the host session (D9). Attribution therefore maps each write to the request most recently delivered to the model in its host session when the write started. A write is never attributed by guesswork: when a verb cannot read its host session key from its own invocation context (host binding table, section 3.2), it binds only if exactly one live host session of its agent exists in the workspace (warning `host_session_inferred`); with none it is refused (`host_session_unknown`), and with more than one it is refused (`host_session_ambiguous`), in both cases unless it carries the trusted recovery or review-backfill pair (original MCP `sessionId` and `requestId`, verified against the server for this workspace and agent, C5); an explicit `requestId` alone never lets a verb without a host session key write. No verb ever targets the workspace-level `current-turn.yaml`.
106: - Ambiguous attribution (operator D9, 2026-10-09: "Refuse when ambiguous"): no host supplies a per-action signal of which request caused a write, so automatic binding applies only while exactly one delivered request is open in the host session. While two or more delivered requests are open (for example R2 absorbed mid-turn while R1 is still open), a write without an explicit `requestId` is refused with `request_ambiguous`, naming the open requests; the model passes `requestId` until all but one are closed. Writes are never attributed by guesswork.

# Copilot Instructions — QBrainAi

**Agent Identity:** When posting to the MCP session log, use the agent's actual identity in Pascal-Case for `sourceType` and the session ID prefix. Do not use inaccurate aliases, lowercase names, or legacy placeholders. Example: `Codex`.
For specific operational instructions (session bootstrap, turn logging lifecycle, helper command order), follow `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`.

## Response Formatting

- Do not use table-style output in responses.
- Use concise bullets or short paragraphs instead.

## Terminal Usage

- Do NOT set focus to the terminal window.
- Do NOT write multiline commands to the terminal; use temporary scripts instead.
- Use **only `pwsh.exe`** (PowerShell 7+). Do not invoke `powershell.exe` (Windows PowerShell 5.1) for scripts, examples, or tooling.

## Session Logging Requirements

- Follow `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` for workflow and helper command order.
- Persist session log changes immediately after each meaningful update; do not batch unsaved turn changes.
- For each turn, include as much detail as available: interpretation, response/status, actions (type/status/filePath), files modified, design decisions, requirements discovered, blockers, and context references.

## Build, Test, Lint

## Architecture

**QBrainAi** is a standalone ASP.NET Core 9 server providing context retrieval, TODO management, session logging, repository operations, and GitHub issue sync for AI agents. It exposes functionality via two transports:

- **HTTP REST API** — Controllers under `src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/Controllers/` (routes at `/qbrainai/*`).
- **MCP Streamable HTTP** — `app.MapMcp("/mcp-transport")` using ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore.
- **MCP STDIO** — `--transport stdio` flag; same tools as HTTP via `McpStdio/FwhMcpTools.cs`.

**Workspace model**: The primary host manages multiple workspaces, each getting its own in-process Kestrel `WebApplication` (not child processes). Workspace config lives in `appsettings.json` under `Mcp:Workspaces` (not in the database). One workspace is the "primary" — served by the host process directly; others get child `WebApplication` instances via `WorkspaceAppFactory`.

**Search pipeline**: Hybrid search combines SQLite FTS5 full-text with HNSW vector similarity (384-dim all-MiniLM-L6-v2 ONNX embeddings). `HybridSearchService` fuses both with BM25 scoring.

**Storage**: EF Core with SQLite (`McpDbContext`). TODO items use a pluggable backend — either YAML file-backed (`TodoService`) or SQLite table-backed (`SqliteTodoService`), selected via `Mcp:TodoStorage:Provider`.

**Multi-instance**: `McpInstanceResolver` overlays per-instance config from `Mcp:Instances:{name}` onto base `Mcp:*` settings.

## Key Conventions

### XML Documentation Required

`TreatWarningsAsErrors` and `GenerateDocumentationFile` are enabled globally in `Directory.Build.props`. All public types and members must have XML doc comments or the build fails (CS1591). Use `/// <inheritdoc />` for interface implementations. Test projects are not exempt: test classes and test methods must include XML docs that state what is being tested, what data/fixtures are used, why that data/fixtures are used, and which requirement IDs are validated.

### Requirement Traceability Comments

All source files reference their FR/TR requirement IDs in doc comments (e.g., `/// <summary>TR-PLANNED-CORE-013: Constructor.</summary>`). When adding new functionality, reference the relevant requirement ID from `docs/Project/Functional-Requirements.md` and `docs/Project/Technical-Requirements.md`.

# Copilot Instructions — QBrainAi

**Agent Identity:** When posting to the MCP session log, use the agent's actual identity in Pascal-Case for `sourceType` and the session ID prefix. Do not use inaccurate aliases, lowercase names, or legacy placeholders. Example: `Codex`.
For specific operational instructions (session bootstrap, turn logging lifecycle, helper command order), follow `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`.

## Response Formatting

- Do not use table-style output in responses.
- Use concise bullets or short paragraphs instead.

## Terminal Usage

- Do NOT set focus to the terminal window.
- Do NOT write multiline commands to the terminal; use temporary scripts instead.
- Use **only `pwsh.exe`** (PowerShell 7+). Do not invoke `powershell.exe` (Windows PowerShell 5.1) for scripts, examples, or tooling.

## Session Logging Requirements

- Follow `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` for workflow and helper command order.
- Persist session log changes immediately after each meaningful update; do not batch unsaved turn changes.
- For each turn, include as much detail as available: interpretation, response/status, actions (type/status/filePath), files modified, design decisions, requirements discovered, blockers, and context references.

## Build, Test, Lint

```powershell
# Build (via Nuke)
./build.ps1 Compile
# or: dotnet build src\QBrainAi.Support.Mcp -c Debug

# Run all unit tests (via Nuke)
./build.ps1 Test
# or individual projects:
# dotnet test tests\QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Tests -c Debug
# dotnet test tests\QBrainAi.Client.Tests -c Debug
# dotnet test tests\Build.Tests -c Debug

# Run integration tests (uses CustomWebApplicationFactory, in-memory EF)
dotnet test tests\QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.IntegrationTests -c Debug

# Run a single test by fully-qualified name
dotnet test tests\QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Tests -c Debug --filter "FullyQualifiedName~TodoServiceTests.QueryAsync_NoFilters_ReturnsAllItems"

# Run tests in a single class
dotnet test tests\QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Tests -c Debug --filter "FullyQualifiedName~TodoServiceTests"

# Validate appsettings config (via Nuke)
./build.ps1 ValidateConfig
# or: pwsh.exe -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File ./scripts/Validate-McpConfig.ps1

# Validate requirements traceability
./build.ps1 ValidateTraceability

# Markdown lint (docs only)
# CI uses markdownlint-cli2 with .markdownlint-cli2.yaml
```

## Architecture

**QBrainAi** is a standalone ASP.NET Core 9 server providing context retrieval, TODO management, session logging, repository operations, and GitHub issue sync for AI agents. It exposes functionality via two transports:

- **HTTP REST API** — Controllers under `src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/Controllers/` (routes at `/qbrainai/*`).
- **MCP Streamable HTTP** — `app.MapMcp("/mcp-transport")` using ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore.
- **MCP STDIO** — `--transport stdio` flag; same tools as HTTP via `McpStdio/FwhMcpTools.cs`.

**Workspace model**: The primary host manages multiple workspaces, each getting its own in-process Kestrel `WebApplication` (not child processes). Workspace config lives in `appsettings.json` under `Mcp:Workspaces` (not in the database). One workspace is the "primary" — served by the host process directly; others get child `WebApplication` instances via `WorkspaceAppFactory`.

**Search pipeline**: Hybrid search combines SQLite FTS5 full-text with HNSW vector similarity (384-dim all-MiniLM-L6-v2 ONNX embeddings). `HybridSearchService` fuses both with BM25 scoring.

**Storage**: EF Core with SQLite (`McpDbContext`). TODO items use a pluggable backend — either YAML file-backed (`TodoService`) or SQLite table-backed (`SqliteTodoService`), selected via `Mcp:TodoStorage:Provider`.

**Multi-instance**: `McpInstanceResolver` overlays per-instance config from `Mcp:Instances:{name}` onto base `Mcp:*` settings.

## Key Conventions

### XML Documentation Required

`TreatWarningsAsErrors` and `GenerateDocumentationFile` are enabled globally in `Directory.Build.props`. All public types and members must have XML doc comments or the build fails (CS1591). Use `/// <inheritdoc />` for interface implementations. Test projects are not exempt: test classes and test methods must include XML docs that state what is being tested, what data/fixtures are used, why that data/fixtures are used, and which requirement IDs are validated.

### Requirement Traceability Comments

All source files reference their FR/TR requirement IDs in doc comments (e.g., `/// <summary>TR-PLANNED-CORE-013: Constructor.</summary>`). When adding new functionality, reference the relevant requirement ID from `docs/Project/Functional-Requirements.md` and `docs/Project/Technical-Requirements.md`.
