95: Turn logging
96: - Every user request (including messages queued mid-turn) is exactly one turn; actions and decisions map to the turn of the request that caused them, determined by the write-attribution rule below (D2). Enforcement of turn-logging correctness is Phase A and ships first.
97: - Plugin turn edits are independent: opening, editing, closing, or canceling one turn never changes another turn's local or server state; concurrent edits to different turns do not interfere.
98: - Unsupported-session failsafe (operator, 2026-10-10: "If QBrain is truly not available, use the failsafe already in the plugin." and, choosing between a failsafe capture and a warn-only Stop, "1"): when a host session fails closed under D6 (`unsupportedSince`), the model's session-log writes for a turn that was already open at that moment go to the plugin's existing failsafe instead of being refused (reviews excepted: they keep their no-failsafe rule and are recorded after the drain through the original pair), so the Stop gate's remedy stays accepted; the captured records drain at the next SessionStart through the trusted recovery flow with the turn's original pair (C5); every mint and every write for any other turn stays refused (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001).
99: - Clear-session closing rule (operator, 2026-10-10, choosing option A over leaving blocked and withdrawn turns open: "A"): clear-session completes each turn that meets the completion policy, fails each withdrawn turn (reason "withdrawn before delivery") and each turn the model marks blocked (with its blocker reason; `failed` requires `requestClass` only, FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002-AC002), and leaves every other turn in progress, reported by requestId with its exact missing items, never fabricating reviews (TR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001-AC001). Definition (catalog cross-reference, not a change to the decision): "marked blocked" means the turn's `blockers` section (the existing decision-list field, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-006-AC001) holds at least one nonblank model-authored entry, read by the clear-session coordinator for that turn by its original (`sessionId`, `requestId`) pair, and the first entry is the fail reason; precedence per turn: withdrawn -> `failTurn` ("withdrawn before delivery"); else blocked -> `failTurn` with the blocker reason (blocked takes precedence over a ready completion); else meets the completion policy -> `completeTurn`; else stays in progress, reported with its exact missing items. Close prerequisites (catalog cross-reference, not a change to the decision): before clear-session fails a withdrawn or blocked turn, the model writes by that turn's original pair, within the same clear-session run and before its session-end step, every prerequisite the plugin and the server require for that close, in the Stop gate remedy order (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC009): a designDecision when the turn has no model evidence (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC002), then a `requestClass` when it is missing or `Unclassified`, judged from the turn's `queryText`; the coordinator then fails the turn with its reason (TR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001-AC001).
100: - Request identity (operator D1, 2026-10-09: "have the server issue a request token when a message arrives"): the server mints every turn's `requestId` when a user message arrives (ingress), through the new mint operation `POST /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/mint`. The mint call carries an idempotency nonce derived from the host's own identity for that message event (host binding table, section 3.2): a host per-prompt id, or a SHA-256 of host event fields that every delivery of that event carries identically. Every delivery of one event therefore sends the same nonce and receives the same token, including network retries and failsafe replay on every host and, on hosts whose nonce is a stable per-message id (codex `turn_id`, grok and grok-bot `promptId`, cline-v2 `runId`, opencode `messageID`) or the bridge's single ordered source (claude-code, claude-cowork), two hook processes started by a doubly registered hook (on copilot and classic cline a second registration is refused before any mint, and a second new equal-field invocation fails closed); two separate user messages (including two intentionally identical prompts) are two events and receive two tokens. On copilot and classic cline, whose event fields include no per-message id, a message whose session, timestamp, and prompt all equal an already minted one is indistinguishable from a redelivery of it, so the host session fails closed under D6 instead of merging or guessing (host binding table, equal-field rule). The host id is only the idempotency key; the turn identity is the server-issued token. There is no prompt-text dedupe window. Every mint comes from a host arrival mechanism (a prompt hook, the arrival bridge, or a host-native hook adapter); no supported host relies on the model to mint. The stop gate's `duplicate_delivery_suspected` warning is a diagnostic only and is never counted as D1 compliance.
101: - Queued-message arrival (operator D5, 2026-10-09: "Arrival bridge"): a message the operator sends while a turn is running is minted when it is enqueued, not when the model later processes it. On hosts that record the enqueue in a transcript (Claude Code), a per-host-session arrival bridge started by the SessionStart hook tails the transcript and follows each queued message through the lifecycle the transcript records. Observed in this workspace's Claude Code transcripts on 2026-10-09: 117 `enqueue`, 79 `dequeue`, 35 `remove` (27 with reason `absorbed_mid_turn`), 2 `popAll`; a normal prompt is `enqueue` then `dequeue` within milliseconds, a mid-turn message is `enqueue` then `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn` when it is injected into the running turn (for example the operator's mid-turn message beginning "write a global memory with the" was removed with `absorbed_mid_turn` at 2026-10-09T14:35:47.730Z), and `popAll` pulls queued text back into the input box. The bridge mints at `enqueue` (state `queued`); the request becomes `delivered` at `dequeue` (applied by the bridge from the transcript itself; on hosts with a bridge the prompt hook neither mints nor claims) or at `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn`; it becomes `withdrawn` at `popAll` or a `remove` with any other or no reason. Task notifications and other system events that the host also enqueues are classified and never minted; on bridge hosts they keep their queue position (`kind: system`), so their `dequeue` never delivers a user request.
102: - Hosts without an arrival mechanism (operator D6, 2026-10-09: "Adapters or unsupported"): a host is supported for turn logging only through an arrival mechanism this plan specifies (a prompt hook that fires at enqueue, the claude-code/claude-cowork arrival bridge, or the classic-cline native-hook adapter); every other host is unsupported until a separately approved adapter exists, and a queue or enqueue event that P0.2 records on such a host becomes a traced follow-up adapter TODO (filed in P0.8) for operator approval (host binding table, section 3.2). A host with no arrival mechanism is declared unsupported for turn logging until it gains one: its plugin reports `turn_logging_unsupported` on every session-log verb and writes nothing (a host session that becomes unsupported after one of its requests was delivered follows the host binding table unsupported-session rule and the 2026-10-10 failsafe decision), and no first-sight minting is used anywhere.
103: - Plugin equivalence (operator D7, 2026-10-09, confirmed in chat "1 yes" for the requirement and its qualification posted by Codex in `MEMORY-PROCESS-007` at 17:48:48Z and 17:52:06Z): all QBrain.AI plugins keep equivalent functionality; shared capabilities, contracts, fixes, and behavior changes go to every plugin; host-specific adaptations preserve equivalent supported behavior; equivalence is limited by what each host's plugin infrastructure can support, no extraordinary effort is spent forcing unworkable equivalence, and each such limit is documented as a feature-specific capability limitation instead of being claimed as equivalent. A D6 `turn_logging_unsupported` host is such a documented limitation. The limitations live in `docs/AGENT-PLUGIN-FEATURE-MATRIX.md` (one row per plugin and feature: supported, adapted, or limited, with the reason and the receipt), first written in P0.8 from the P0.2 receipts, updated in A9 and S11, and checked by a docs contract test.
104: - Ninth plugin (operator D8, 2026-10-09: "2 yes"): `mcpserver-grok-bot-plugin` is in scope like the other eight.
105: - Write attribution (operator D2, 2026-10-09: tie each write to its request automatically through the agent app's hooks): every verb invocation is bound to one request automatically from host context, without the model naming it: the binding is the write target of the invoking host session at the moment the invocation starts, captured once and stored immutably with that invocation (its persist record and failsafe record), so a later message never retargets an invocation already started. A host session's write target is the request most recently delivered to the model in that host session: a prompt the host hands to the model as a new turn (the prompt hook on hosts without a bridge, or the bridge's `dequeue` delivery), or a queued message absorbed into the running turn (`absorbed_mid_turn`). Minting alone never moves the write target, so work the model is still doing for request R1 after R2 is enqueued stays on R1 until R2 is delivered. Explicit `requestId` remains accepted as an override, for example to continue R1 work after R2 was absorbed, and it is required while two or more delivered requests are open in the host session (D9). Attribution therefore maps each write to the request most recently delivered to the model in its host session when the write started. A write is never attributed by guesswork: when a verb cannot read its host session key from its own invocation context (host binding table, section 3.2), it binds only if exactly one live host session of its agent exists in the workspace (warning `host_session_inferred`); with none it is refused (`host_session_unknown`), and with more than one it is refused (`host_session_ambiguous`), in both cases unless it carries the trusted recovery or review-backfill pair (original MCP `sessionId` and `requestId`, verified against the server for this workspace and agent, C5); an explicit `requestId` alone never lets a verb without a host session key write. No verb ever targets the workspace-level `current-turn.yaml`.
106: - Ambiguous attribution (operator D9, 2026-10-09: "Refuse when ambiguous"): no host supplies a per-action signal of which request caused a write, so automatic binding applies only while exactly one delivered request is open in the host session. While two or more delivered requests are open (for example R2 absorbed mid-turn while R1 is still open), a write without an explicit `requestId` is refused with `request_ambiguous`, naming the open requests; the model passes `requestId` until all but one are closed. Writes are never attributed by guesswork.
107: - Copilot duplicate deliveries (operator D11, 2026-10-09: "Supported only if single hook"): Copilot gives no stable per-prompt id and separately registered hooks may see different `timestamp` values, so Copilot turn logging is supported only while the plugin's duplicate check proves exactly one MCP prompt hook across all Copilot hook sources; otherwise the Copilot prompt hook reports `turn_logging_unsupported` before any mint, and the condition is a D7 documented limitation until fixed. One Copilot prompt therefore never becomes two turns.
108: - Node runtime floor (operator D12, 2026-10-09: "Keep Node 18/20"), superseded for core code by the 2026-10-11 PowerShell-only ruling: no code of this plan runs on Node except the logic-free TypeScript-host adapters, which keep each host's declared engine unchanged (mcpserver-cline-plugin, mcpserver-cline-v2-plugin, and mcpserver-opencode-plugin `>=18`; the Cline application's own `node >=22` is unaffected). Exact review scores are validated and carried by the PowerShell core's raw-lexeme rules (S8); the adapters never parse a score (C10).
109: 
110: Request class
111: - Turn scalar `requestClass`: `Code` | `Docs` | `Chore` (case-insensitive in, canonical PascalCase out, anything else rejected). Required, enforced at transition to `completed` or `failed`, not at creation (hooks create turns before the agent can classify). Legacy rows backfilled to `Unclassified` (readable; never accepted on new writes from agent surfaces).
112: 
113: Review record (shared by `agentReview` and `hostileReview`)
114: - Fields: `status` (`Unnecessary` | `Unstarted` | `Running` | `Pass` | `Fail` | `Other`), `otherNotes`, `correctness`, `completeness` (lossless decimal 0..1), `correctnessThreshold`, `completenessThreshold` (server-stamped, read-only), `reasons` (string[]), `reviewer`, `reviewedAt` (UTC), `requestJsonlPath`, `responseJsonlPath`. No `passed` bool.
115: - One record per kind per turn; latest write wins.
116: - Server creates both at turn creation as `Unstarted`. `hostileReview` flips to `Unnecessary` when `requestClass` becomes `Chore`, and back to `Unstarted` if the class changes away while still `Unnecessary`. Records past `Unstarted`/`Unnecessary` are never auto-changed. Legacy turns are backfilled `agentReview=Unstarted`, `hostileReview=Unstarted`. (Catalog cross-references, not a change to the decision: the flip and its reverse apply only to in-progress turns, FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-006-AC002 and UC-4; a reset restores the creation default for the turn's current class, FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-001-AC004.)
117: - `otherNotes` with text is rejected unless `status` is `Other`.
118: - Strict per-status fields: `Unnecessary`/`Unstarted` carry no scores, reasons, reviewer, timestamps, or paths; `Running` requires `reviewer`, forbids scores; `Pass`/`Fail` require `correctness`, `completeness`, `reviewer`, `reviewedAt`; `hostileReview` `Pass`/`Fail` also require `requestJsonlPath` and `responseJsonlPath`; `Other` requires non-empty `otherNotes` (the Other reason; operator D4, 2026-10-09: "Other requires Other Reason be populated") and allows optional scores, `reasons`, `reviewer`, `reviewedAt`, and receipt paths. `Unnecessary` is server-managed only.
119: - Thresholds: `Mcp:SessionLog:ReviewThresholds:{Agent|Hostile}:{Correctness|Completeness}` (decimal 0..1, per instance through `McpInstanceResolver` overrides), default 0.98, inclusive (score >= threshold passes). Pass requires both scores to meet their thresholds. The server derives `Pass`/`Fail`; a supplied `Pass`/`Fail` that contradicts the derivation is rejected (422 `review_status_conflict`); omitting status lets the server derive it. `Other` is never derived. Thresholds in force are stamped on the record.
120: - Names stay `correctness`/`completeness`. HV tooling maps `accuracy` -> `correctness` and integer percent -> decimal/100.
226: ### 3.2 Host binding table and TypeScript-host adapter contract
227: 
228: Host binding table (locks the D1 nonce source, the D5 arrival source, and the D2 host session key per host; every turn token is still minted by the server). Rules common to all hosts:
229: - Nonce: computed from the event itself, never from the hook process, so every delivery of one event yields the same nonce; a value outside `^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,64}$` is replaced by the 64 lowercase hex characters of its SHA-256. Equal-field rule (copilot and classic cline, whose nonce hashes event fields with no per-message id): under `turn-open.lock`, a new prompt-hook invocation whose nonce already has a failsafe mint record or a `pending-<nonce>` turn in that host session, or whose mint returns `merged`, cannot be told apart from a separate message with equal session, timestamp, and prompt, so it mints and binds nothing and the host session fails closed under D6 exactly as the bridge does for an unattributable record (`unsupportedSince: { causeNonce, causeOperation: prompt_hook, reason: indistinguishable_arrival }` with the session-level envelope; every session-log verb then reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and writes nothing to the server until the session ends, except that writes for a turn already open at that moment go to the plugin failsafe under the unsupported-session failsafe rule, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001; its open turns are listed at the next SessionStart). A network retry or failsafe replay of a stored mint record is a drain of that record, not a new invocation, and reuses its nonce without failing closed.
230: - Unsupported-session rule (D6; operator option 1 of 2026-10-10): every check that makes a host session report `turn_logging_unsupported` after one of its requests was delivered records `unsupportedSince` with the session-level envelope in `turn-state.yaml` in the same atomic replace that makes the session unsupported, with `reason` set to that check's code: `queue_removal_ambiguous` (bridge), `indistinguishable_arrival` (equal-field rule), `arrival_bridge_format_unrecognized` (an unknown queue operation, a record missing a required field, or a transcript shorter than `appliedThroughOffset`), `duplicate_prompt_hook` (the copilot or classic-cline single-registration check starts failing; the first verb or hook in that host session that observes it records it), or, for any other D6 check, its own reason code; plus `causeOffset` or `causeNonce` where the cause has one, else `detectedAtUtc`. Whatever the reason, the unsupported-session failsafe of FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001 then applies: writes for a turn of that host session still in progress when `unsupportedSince` was recorded (a delivered open request, or a `withdrawn` queue entry still `in_progress`, addressed by its original pair; a minted request still `queued` is not covered and stays a warning) are captured, and every mint and every other write is refused. The state lasts until the host session ends, or until a SessionStart clears its cause where the cause's own rule allows (the bridge restarting on a valid transcript); the captured records drain at that SessionStart. A host that is unsupported from its first event mints nothing, has no open turn, and records no `unsupportedSince`.
231: - P0.2 gating rule (D6, D7): every case, gate, or live assertion that needs a host's arrival mechanism or a P0.2-probed host field runs only when that host's P0.2 row passed; when the row failed or was unavailable, the host's D6 case `<Host>P02NotPassedTurnLoggingUnsupportedZeroMintsZeroWrites` runs instead in the same slice (A3: `ClaudeCodeP02NotPassedTurnLoggingUnsupportedZeroMintsZeroWrites`, `GrokP02NotPassedTurnLoggingUnsupportedZeroMintsZeroWrites`, `GrokBotP02NotPassedTurnLoggingUnsupportedZeroMintsZeroWrites`, `CopilotP02NotPassedTurnLoggingUnsupportedZeroMintsZeroWrites`, `CoworkP02NotPassedTurnLoggingUnsupportedZeroMintsZeroWrites`; A8: `ClineP02NotPassedTurnLoggingUnsupportedZeroMintsZeroWrites`, `ClineV2P02NotPassedTurnLoggingUnsupportedZeroMintsZeroWrites`, `OpenCodeP02NotPassedTurnLoggingUnsupportedZeroMintsZeroWrites`), and every live check excludes that host with its P0.2 receipt (codex excepted: a failed or unavailable codex row, or a codex enqueue-versus-processing result of "only when processed", stops P0 instead, because every HV reviewer persists its own turn through the Codex plugin; host binding table, codex). 227: 
228: Host binding table (locks the D1 nonce source, the D5 arrival source, and the D2 host session key per host; every turn token is still minted by the server). Rules common to all hosts:
229: - Nonce: computed from the event itself, never from the hook process, so every delivery of one event yields the same nonce; a value outside `^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,64}$` is replaced by the 64 lowercase hex characters of its SHA-256. Equal-field rule (copilot and classic cline, whose nonce hashes event fields with no per-message id): under `turn-open.lock`, a new prompt-hook invocation whose nonce already has a failsafe mint record or a `pending-<nonce>` turn in that host session, or whose mint returns `merged`, cannot be told apart from a separate message with equal session, timestamp, and prompt, so it mints and binds nothing and the host session fails closed under D6 exactly as the bridge does for an unattributable record (`unsupportedSince: { causeNonce, causeOperation: prompt_hook, reason: indistinguishable_arrival }` with the session-level envelope; every session-log verb then reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and writes nothing to the server until the session ends, except that writes for a turn already open at that moment go to the plugin failsafe under the unsupported-session failsafe rule, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001; its open turns are listed at the next SessionStart). A network retry or failsafe replay of a stored mint record is a drain of that record, not a new invocation, and reuses its nonce without failing closed.
230: - Unsupported-session rule (D6; operator option 1 of 2026-10-10): every check that makes a host session report `turn_logging_unsupported` after one of its requests was delivered records `unsupportedSince` with the session-level envelope in `turn-state.yaml` in the same atomic replace that makes the session unsupported, with `reason` set to that check's code: `queue_removal_ambiguous` (bridge), `indistinguishable_arrival` (equal-field rule), `arrival_bridge_format_unrecognized` (an unknown queue operation, a record missing a required field, or a transcript shorter than `appliedThroughOffset`), `duplicate_prompt_hook` (the copilot or classic-cline single-registration check starts failing; the first verb or hook in that host session that observes it records it), or, for any other D6 check, its own reason code; plus `causeOffset` or `causeNonce` where the cause has one, else `detectedAtUtc`. Whatever the reason, the unsupported-session failsafe of FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001 then applies: writes for a turn of that host session still in progress when `unsupportedSince` was recorded (a delivered open request, or a `withdrawn` queue entry still `in_progress`, addressed by its original pair; a minted request still `queued` is not covered and stays a warning) are captured, and every mint and every other write is refused. 229: - Nonce: computed from the event itself, never from the hook process, so every delivery of one event yields the same nonce; a value outside `^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,64}$` is replaced by the 64 lowercase hex characters of its SHA-256. Equal-field rule (copilot and classic cline, whose nonce hashes event fields with no per-message id): under `turn-open.lock`, a new prompt-hook invocation whose nonce already has a failsafe mint record or a `pending-<nonce>` turn in that host session, or whose mint returns `merged`, cannot be told apart from a separate message with equal session, timestamp, and prompt, so it mints and binds nothing and the host session fails closed under D6 exactly as the bridge does for an unattributable record (`unsupportedSince: { causeNonce, causeOperation: prompt_hook, reason: indistinguishable_arrival }` with the session-level envelope; every session-log verb then reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and writes nothing to the server until the session ends, except that writes for a turn already open at that moment go to the plugin failsafe under the unsupported-session failsafe rule, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001; its open turns are listed at the next SessionStart). A network retry or failsafe replay of a stored mint record is a drain of that record, not a new invocation, and reuses its nonce without failing closed.
230: - Unsupported-session rule (D6; operator option 1 of 2026-10-10): every check that makes a host session report `turn_logging_unsupported` after one of its requests was delivered records `unsupportedSince` with the session-level envelope in `turn-state.yaml` in the same atomic replace that makes the session unsupported, with `reason` set to that check's code: `queue_removal_ambiguous` (bridge), `indistinguishable_arrival` (equal-field rule), `arrival_bridge_format_unrecognized` (an unknown queue operation, a record missing a required field, or a transcript shorter than `appliedThroughOffset`), `duplicate_prompt_hook` (the copilot or classic-cline single-registration check starts failing; the first verb or hook in that host session that observes it records it), or, for any other D6 check, its own reason code; plus `causeOffset` or `causeNonce` where the cause has one, else `detectedAtUtc`. Whatever the reason, the unsupported-session failsafe of FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001 then applies: writes for a turn of that host session still in progress when `unsupportedSince` was recorded (a delivered open request, or a `withdrawn` queue entry still `in_progress`, addressed by its original pair; a minted request still `queued` is not covered and stays a warning) are captured, and every mint and every other write is refused. The state lasts until the host session ends, or until a SessionStart clears its cause where the cause's own rule allows (the bridge restarting on a valid transcript); the captured records drain at that SessionStart. 398: - `TurnStatus`: `IsTerminal(status)` is true for `completed`, `failed`, `closed`, `canceled`, and `cancelled` (develop's set, `SessionLogService.cs:1355-1361`); every "terminal" and "nonterminal" in this document means this predicate. Agent surfaces (REST, MCP, client, REPL, plugin) accept the statuses `in_progress`, `completed`, `failed`, and `canceled` on writes (the legacy spelling `cancelled` stays accepted, as FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-002 relies on); a write naming `closed` is refused with 400 `validation_error` (operator, 2026-10-12, answer "Refuse from agent surfaces (Recommended)"); server-internal writers and existing rows keep `closed`.
399: - `TurnLocator`: validates the session id and, when the unit addresses a turn, the request id (`SessionLogIdentifierValidator`, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/SessionLogIdentifierValidator.cs:8`), finds the session by (workspace, agent, sessionId) and the turn by (session, requestId). It returns typed results; each surface maps them to its existing body, listed in the unit's error list. Every unit that addresses a session or a turn, including the review units and the agent-context units that name a turn, calls it with the same key; an agent-context request that names a turn carries `agent`, `sessionId`, and `requestId`.

414: - `TurnWritePipeline`: the one write path of every turn-writing unit (SubmitSessionLogCommand per turn, UpsertSessionTurnCommand, PatchSessionTurnCommand, ReplaceSessionTurnCommand, CompleteSessionTurnCommand, FailSessionTurnCommand), run inside SerializableWrite. Modes: `Submit` (policy TerminalTurnOutcomeGuard first; the completion gate's missing items are collected and the submission is rejected once after every turn is evaluated), `Merge` (additive; insert when absent; Upsert, Patch), `Replace` (whole replacement; the turn must exist), and the status overrides `Complete` and `Fail` (Merge with the status set). The single-turn modes reject at the first refusal. The insert-when-absent race is IdempotentCreate with policy `MergeInto` (one retry mechanism, no separate race step). Review records carried in the turn body pass policy ReviewValidation (section 5.3) before RequestClassification. The completion gate runs when the write moves the turn into `completed` or `failed`, or when a Replace carries `completed` or `failed` (FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002-AC004), never on any other write that only enriches an already terminal turn. The QBAgent terminal compliance check (`ValidateTerminalTurnCompliance`, `SessionLogService.cs:1329`) runs in the single-turn modes only, as today. Single-turn modes read only their session row and their turn (turn-level isolation); the session summary refresh runs after the turn commits, as its own short write whose failure never fails the turn write. Outputs: the turn id (single-turn modes) or the per-turn outcome (`Submit`). Typed failures, mapped by each surface to the bodies its unit lists: `InvalidIdentifier`, `SessionNotFound` (never in `Submit` mode, which opens or upserts its session first), `TurnNotFound`, `InvalidPayload`, `ReviewInvalid` (with the policy ReviewValidation code), `RequestClassInvalid`, `CompletionGateMissing` (with the missing items), and the SerializableWrite conflict.

443: #### 3.5.4 Scoring and reviews
444: 
445: - `ScoreLexeme` and `ScoreLexemeJsonConverter` (namespace `QBrainAi.Client.Scoring`; the rule of section 3.4, Scores): validates a score lexeme (pattern, at most 28 fractional digits, value in [0, 1]) and parses it exactly; errors 400 `review_score_format`, `review_score_precision`, `review_score_out_of_range`. The converter validates at deserialization, so an invalid score is refused before any lookup (an invalid score on an unknown turn is 400, not 404). The REPL's lossless normalizer calls `ScoreLexeme` for the review keys (`agentReview`, `hostileReview`, `recordReview`) and for the agent-context grade keys (`correctness` and `completeness` of `RecordModelGradeAsync`), so `verdict_match` (section 6.3) compares lexemes that no hop has re-serialized. The PowerShell core's copy (`Protect-ReplLosslessScalars`) is a language boundary, kept in step by the golden contract test of the review contract.
446: - `ScoreVerdict` (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Scoring`): derives `Pass` or `Fail` from two scores against their thresholds, inclusive (score >= threshold), and returns the thresholds in force for stamping. Parameters: the thresholds and an optional floor and count rule. Phase B reviews use the configured thresholds in [0, 1] and refuse a supplied `Pass` or `Fail` that contradicts the derivation with 422 `review_status_conflict`; agent-context grades and the trust decision apply `max(configured, 0.98)` and require zero FAIL and zero UNKNOWN findings. Used by policy ReviewValidation (RecordSessionTurnReviewCommand and review records in turn bodies), policy HvVerdictMapping, RunDeterministicGradeCommand, RecordModelGradeCommand, and DecideAgentResponseTrustCommand (which re-derives from the stored scores with the floor).
447: - `ReviewDefaults` (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Reviews`): the default review status for a kind and class: `agentReview` `Unstarted`; `hostileReview` `Unnecessary` when the class is `Chore`, otherwise `Unstarted`. Applied at turn insert, by a section reset, by the Chore flip of policy RequestClassification (only a record still at a default status, only on a nonterminal turn), and by the S3 backfill.

      "description": "Vote (+1 / -1) on Question and Answer with one-vote-per-user enforcement. A given actor may hold at most one active vote per entity (Question or Answer). Submitting the same vote a second time is idempotent (returns the current state, no counter change, no new audit row). Submitting the opposite vote replaces the prior vote (counter adjusts by +/- 2; an audit row is written for the change). An actor may explicitly revoke their vote (counter adjusts by -1 or +1; audit row recorded). Voter identity is the value resolved by `IQaAuthorResolver`. The Question/Answer rows still store a denormalized counter for fast reads; the authoritative per-voter state lives in a `QaVoteEntity` table with a unique constraint (TR-MCP-QA-032). Voter identity and every vote transition (apply, change, revoke) appear in the audit history (TR-MCP-QA-019), and a voter-history endpoint exposes them (TR-MCP-QA-031)."
    },

The marker is regenerated in full on every server start and carries the per-workspace API key that rotates on each restart, so an archived copy preserves no recoverable state of value while leaving an expired credential on disk. Each graceful shutdown currently leaves one tombstone permanently: as of 2026-07-20 the QBrainAi workspace held 19 of them, 587,033 bytes, dated 2026-07-08 through 2026-07-16, every one containing the apiKey that was live when it was written. TR-MCP-DB-003 (soft deletes for persistent MCP data) governs persistent MCP domain rows and their relationships; it does not extend to regenerated filesystem artifacts, and applying it to the marker was an over-generalization.       "createdAt": "2026-10-13T13:04:32.6151334-05:00",
      "description": "Vote (+1 / -1) on Question and Answer with one-vote-per-user enforcement. A given actor may hold at most one active vote per entity (Question or Answer). Submitting the same vote a second time is idempotent (returns the current state, no counter change, no new audit row). Submitting the opposite vote replaces the prior vote (counter adjusts by +/- 2; an audit row is written for the change). An actor may explicitly revoke their vote (counter adjusts by -1 or +1; audit row recorded). Voter identity is the value resolved by `IQaAuthorResolver`. The Question/Answer rows still store a denormalized counter for fast reads; the authoritative per-voter state lives in a `QaVoteEntity` table with a unique constraint (TR-MCP-QA-032). Voter identity and every vote transition (apply, change, revoke) appear in the audit history (TR-MCP-QA-019), and a voter-history endpoint exposes them (TR-MCP-QA-031)."
    },

      "description": "Removing the AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml workspace marker must delete the file. It must not rename the marker to an AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml.deleted-{timestamp} archive copy that is never reclaimed. The marker is regenerated in full on every server start and carries the per-workspace API key that rotates on each restart, so an archived copy preserves no recoverable state of value while leaving an expired credential on disk. Each graceful shutdown currently leaves one tombstone permanently: as of 2026-07-20 the QBrainAi workspace held 19 of them, 587,033 bytes, dated 2026-07-08 through 2026-07-16, every one containing the apiKey that was live when it was written. TR-MCP-DB-003 (soft deletes for persistent MCP data) governs persistent MCP domain rows and their relationships; it does not extend to regenerated filesystem artifacts, and applying it to the marker was an over-generalization. The same rule applies to the legacy .mcp-server.yaml and .mcp-server.json markers removed alongside it."
    },

    - "Each TEST id mirrors its TR. P0 creates each record with the title and statement below (exactly: the title is the row text after its id up to ` Tests:`, without its final period; in the statement, <AC list> is the row's Validates and Also validates lists with ranges such as AC001..AC004 expanded, and <test classes> is its Tests: list); the statement is \"Validates <AC list> with <test classes>; every listed new or changed AC has a RED receipt before implementation and a green receipt at the slice gate, and every listed baseline-green AC has a green receipt.\" Every record carries the same three ACs, with its own id prefix: `<TESTID>-AC001` every listed new or changed FR and TR AC has at least one named test that failed (RED) before implementation and passes after, and every listed baseline-green AC has a named test that passes; `<TESTID>-AC002` the mocks-green run and its negative check are recorded on the slice TODO; `<TESTID>-AC003` the listed suites run with zero failures and zero skips in the slice gate. (TEST-SUPPORT-024 uses `ac-1`..`ac-3` with the same texts, matching its family.) Span and satisfaction: a TEST record belongs to the slices in its TR's bracket, every slice labelled in parentheses in its row (for example `(S5)`), and every slice, earlier or later, whose task line names one of its cases or test suites. So TEST-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-008 spans S1, S5, S6, S8, S9, and S10 (S5 and S6 name its golden-map case, S10 its real-gate cases), TEST-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-009 spans S8, S9, and S11 (whose task names `SessionLogReviewDocsContractTests`), and TEST-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-001 spans S1, S3, S4, S5, and S6. Each slice's gate runs the cases that slice owns plus those of every earlier slice in the span, and the record's three ACs are set satisfied only when the last slice of its span completes. Every case a row names is owned by a slice of that span. Where an AC's bracket names several surfaces, each TEST covers the surfaces its own span implements, and the other surfaces are covered by the TESTs of the slices that implement them (a row says so explicitly where it hands one off, as in \"via TEST-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-004\")."

    - "UC-1 Log each user request as exactly one turn. Actors: Operator, agent host (any of the nine), plugin hooks or tools, model. Precondition: workspace trusted (marker signature and health nonce verified). Basic flow: operator submits a prompt; on a prompt-hook or adapter host the hook classifies it as a user request, takes the turn-open lock, derives the nonce from the event (host binding table), asks the server to mint the requestId (the server opens the turn), and records the token as the host session's write target at once; on a bridge host (claude-code, claude-cowork) the arrival bridge mints from the transcript `enqueue` record (state `queued`) and the request becomes the write target at its `dequeue`, or at an `absorbed_mid_turn` removal (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC009, -AC010); the request enters the stop ledger when it is delivered (at once on prompt-hook and adapter hosts; at its `dequeue` or `absorbed_mid_turn` removal on bridge hosts), never at mint; every verb the model invokes is bound automatically to the host session's write target at invocation start; model closes the turn. Alternate flows: the mint call is retried or replayed and returns the same requestId; a doubly registered hook delivers the event twice and both deliveries get the same requestId (only on hosts whose nonce is a stable per-message id or the bridge's single ordered source; on copilot and classic cline a second registration is refused before any mint, and a second new equal-field invocation fails the host session closed under the equal-field rule, while a stored mint retry or failsafe drain reuses its nonce); the server is unreachable and a provisional `pending-<nonce>` turn is rebound on drain; an identical prompt sent again later is a new event and opens a second turn; background event is skipped (on a bridge host it keeps its queue position as an unminted system entry, so its `dequeue` delivers nothing); operator sends a message mid-turn, the arrival bridge mints its turn at enqueue without touching the running turn or the write target, the message is delivered (absorbed into the running turn, or dequeued) and from then on, while the earlier request is still open, an unqualified write is refused with `request_ambiguous` (D9) and the model names the requestId of each write; once the earlier request is closed, unqualified writes bind to the delivered request; the operator pulls a queued message back (`popAll`) before delivery, the request is withdrawn, and the stop gate asks the model to fail it; a verb without a host session key in a workspace with two live sessions is refused rather than guessed; a subagent's hooks fire and leave this session's turns unchanged; while two delivered requests are open an unqualified verb is refused with `request_ambiguous` and the model names the requestId (D9); on Copilot with more than one MCP prompt hook registered the hook reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and mints nothing (D11); on a host with no arrival mechanism every session-log verb reports `turn_logging_unsupported` (D6). Realizes FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001, -002, -003, -007, -008; updated FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-001, FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-002, FR-MCP-REPL-010, FR-MCP-TRIAGESTORE-001."

Basic flow: model records actions/decisions (incl. via `designDecisions`) and closes each turn; Stop hook finds all closed with evidence and passes, clearing the ledger. Alternate: a turn is open (including one whose close the plugin refused for missing model evidence) or its most recent close was refused by the server's completion gate, the Stop hook blocks with the reason and the accepted remedy; a turn closed without evidence by another surface is only warned and never closes turns itself. Every delivery of one event therefore sends the same nonce and receives the same token, including network retries and failsafe replay on every host and, on hosts whose nonce is a stable per-message id (codex `turn_id`, grok and grok-bot `promptId`, cline-v2 `runId`, opencode `messageID`) or the bridge's single ordered source (claude-code, claude-cowork), two hook processes started by a doubly registered hook (on copilot and classic cline a second registration is refused before any mint, and a second new equal-field invocation fails closed); two separate user messages (including two intentionally identical prompts) are two events and receive two tokens. On copilot and classic cline, whose event fields include no per-message id, a message whose session, timestamp, and prompt all equal an already minted one is indistinguishable from a redelivery of it, so the host session fails closed under D6 instead of merging or guessing (host binding table, equal-field rule). The host id is only the idempotency key; the turn identity is the server-issued token. There is no prompt-text dedupe window. Every mint comes from a host arrival mechanism (a prompt hook, the arrival bridge, or a host-native hook adapter); no supported host relies on the model to mint. The stop gate's `duplicate_delivery_suspected` warning is a diagnostic only and is never counted as D1 compliance."
    - "- Queued-message arrival (operator D5, 2026-10-09: \"Arrival bridge\"): a message the operator sends while a turn is running is minted when it is enqueued, not when the model later processes it. On hosts that record the enqueue in a transcript (Claude Code), a per-host-session arrival bridge started by the SessionStart hook tails the transcript and follows each queued message through the lifecycle the transcript records. Observed in this workspace's Claude Code transcripts on 2026-10-09: 117 `enqueue`, 79 `dequeue`, 35 `remove` (27 with reason `absorbed_mid_turn`), 2 `popAll`; a normal prompt is `enqueue` then `dequeue` within milliseconds, a mid-turn message is `enqueue` then `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn` when it is injected into the running turn (for example the operator's mid-turn message beginning \"write a global memory with the\" was removed with `absorbed_mid_turn` at 2026-10-09T14:35:47.730Z), and `popAll` pulls queued text back into the input box. The bridge mints at `enqueue` (state `queued`); the request becomes `delivered` at `dequeue` (applied by the bridge from the transcript itself; on hosts with a bridge the prompt hook neither mints nor claims) or at `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn`; it becomes `withdrawn` at `popAll` or a `remove` with any other or no reason. Task notifications and other system events that the host also enqueues are classified and never minted; on bridge hosts they keep their queue position (`kind: system`), so their `dequeue` never delivers a user request."

A host with no arrival mechanism is declared unsupported for turn logging until it gains one: its plugin reports `turn_logging_unsupported` on every session-log verb and writes nothing (a host session that becomes unsupported after one of its requests was delivered follows the host binding table unsupported-session rule and the 2026-10-10 failsafe decision), and no first-sight minting is used anywhere.'

    - "- Write attribution (operator D2, 2026-10-09: tie each write to its request automatically through the agent app's hooks): every verb invocation is bound to one request automatically from host context, without the model naming it: the binding is the write target of the invoking host session at the moment the invocation starts, captured once and stored immutably with that invocation (its persist record and failsafe record), so a later message never retargets an invocation already started. A host session's write target is the request most recently delivered to the model in that host session: a prompt the host hands to the model as a new turn (the prompt hook on hosts without a bridge, or the bridge's `dequeue` delivery), or a queued message absorbed into the running turn (`absorbed_mid_turn`). Minting alone never moves the write target, so work the model is still doing for request R1 after R2 is enqueued stays on R1 until R2 is delivered. Explicit `requestId` remains accepted as an override, for example to continue R1 work after R2 was absorbed, and it is required while two or more delivered requests are open in the host session (D9). Attribution therefore maps each write to the request most recently delivered to the model in its host session when the write started. A write is never attributed by guesswork: when a verb cannot read its host session key from its own invocation context (host binding table), it binds only if exactly one live host session of its agent exists in the workspace (warning `host_session_inferred`); with none it is refused (`host_session_unknown`), and with more than one it is refused (`host_session_ambiguous`), in both cases unless it carries the trusted recovery or review-backfill pair (original MCP `sessionId` and `requestId`, verified against the server for this workspace and agent, C5); an explicit `requestId` alone never lets a verb without a host session key write. No verb ever targets the workspace-level `current-turn.yaml`."
    - '- Ambiguous attribution (operator D9, 2026-10-09: "Refuse when ambiguous"): no host supplies a per-action signal of which request caused a write, so automatic binding applies only while exactly one delivered request is open in the host session. While two or more delivered requests are open (for example R2 absorbed mid-turn while R1 is still open), a write without an explicit `requestId` is refused with `request_ambiguous`, naming the open requests; the model passes `requestId` until all but one are closed. Writes are never attributed by guesswork.'

229: - Nonce: computed from the event itself, never from the hook process, so every delivery of one event yields the same nonce; a value outside `^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,64}$` is replaced by the 64 lowercase hex characters of its SHA-256. A network retry or failsafe replay of a stored mint record is a drain of that record, not a new invocation, and reuses its nonce without failing closed.
230: - Unsupported-session rule (D6; operator option 1 of 2026-10-10): every check that makes a host session report `turn_logging_unsupported` after one of its requests was delivered records `unsupportedSince` with the session-level envelope in `turn-state.yaml` in the same atomic replace that makes the session unsupported, with `reason` set to that check's code: `queue_removal_ambiguous` (bridge), `indistinguishable_arrival` (equal-field rule), `arrival_bridge_format_unrecognized` (an unknown queue operation, a record missing a required field, or a transcript shorter than `appliedThroughOffset`), `duplicate_prompt_hook` (the copilot or classic-cline single-registration check starts failing; the first verb or hook in that host session that observes it records it), or, for any other D6 check, its own reason code; plus `causeOffset` or `causeNonce` where the cause has one, else `detectedAtUtc`. 378: - `ReadableKeyAllocator` (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage.Keys`): allocates the human-readable keys of section 3 (Identifiers). Strategy `NextOrdinal` (`<prefix><parent>-<nn>`, highest stored suffix within the key's unique index scope plus one; the agent-context keys `pkg-`, `rsp-`, and `grd-` under their record parent, `rel-` under its type and timestamp, and `hvr-` under its session and timestamp with `-<nn>` appended only from the second key of the same second, each with the shortened parent id rule and the formats of section 6.3) or `RandomHex` (`req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<8 hex>`, the Phase A minter). `NextOrdinal` reads past the soft-delete filter, so a deleted record's suffix is never allocated again (`ReadableKeyAllocatorSoftDeletedSuffixNeverReused`). A collision on the key's unique index declares a retry to SerializableWrite with the next candidate. The Phase A minter states its own bound and exhaustion outcome to SerializableWrite for request-id collisions only: today's six attempts and 500 `mint_collision_exhausted` (InsertMintedTurnWithRetry, section 4.2); its transient conflicts keep the default bound and exit; agent-context keys use SerializableWrite's default bound (four attempts), then 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true`.
379: - `PagedQuery` and `PageBounds` (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage.Paging`) with the wire type `PageResult<TItem>` (namespace `QBrainAi.Client.Paging`, fields `totalCount`, `limit`, `offset`, `items`): counts the matches and reads one page in the caller's stable order. `PageBounds` carries the policy: `Clamp` (QuerySessionLogsQuery, today's behavior: limit default 100, clamped to 1..1000, a negative offset read as 0, `SessionLogService.cs:476-477`) or `Refuse` (every agent-context query and RetrieveAgentContextCandidatesQuery's `limit`: limit 1..1000, default 50, offset at least 0, otherwise 400 `validation_error` with `details.field` `limit` or `offset`). The four agent-context page types of section 6.4 are `PageResult<TItem>`.
380: 
381: ```mermaid
382: flowchart TD
383:     S(["PagedQuery: limit, offset, PageBounds, stable order"]) --> P{"PageBounds policy?"}
384:     P -->|Clamp| C["Default the limit when absent, clamp it to the bounds, read a negative offset as 0"]
385:     P -->|Refuse| V{"Limit and offset within the bounds?"}
386:     V -->|no| E(["400 validation_error, details.field limit or offset"])
387:     V -->|yes| Q["Count the matches, read one page in the stable order"]
388:     C --> Q
389:     Q --> R(["PageResult: totalCount, limit, offset, items"])
390: ```
391: 
392: - `ClassifiedErrorException` and `ErrorCodes` (namespace `QBrainAi.Client.Errors`): every new handler fails with `Result<T>.Failure(new ClassifiedErrorException(code, status, message, details, retryable))` (`src/QBrainAi.Cqrs/Result.cs:50`); `ErrorCodes` is the one table of codes with their HTTP status and retryable flag, read by the server, the REPL envelope, and the plugin's receipt mapping (C9). `McpErrorClassifier` (`src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/Services/McpErrorClassifier.cs:14`) maps `ClassifiedErrorException` to the `ClassifiedError` problem+json body and the MCP tool error in one branch; it gains no per-feature branch. Retryable codes: transport outage and degraded persistence (503 `backend_unavailable`), a busy store (503 `persistence_error` with `retryable: true`, today's answer, `McpErrorClassifier.cs:129-139`), and 409 `conflict` when `retryable` is true (SerializableWrite exhausted, key allocation exhausted); every other code is final, including the REPL client-policy codes `transaction_degraded` and `mutation_not_transactional` (`ClientMutationPolicy.cs:203-218`), which `ErrorCodes` lists. The REPL classifier carries a server `ClassifiedError` answer through at every status: its `code`, `message`, `retryable`, and `details` reach the REPL envelope unchanged, where today only a 503 passes the server's code through and `conflict` is forced to `retryable: false` (`src/QBrainAi.Repl.Core/ReplMcpErrorClassifier.cs:60-95`), and any other answer becomes a classifier code or `method_invocation_error` (`src/QBrainAi.Repl.Core/ReplCommandDispatcher.cs:3346-3370`); so the plugin sees the completion-gate token, the review and agent-context codes, and the server's retryable flag (`ReplClassifierConflictRetryableTrueKept`, `ReplClassifierServerClassifiedErrorKeepsCodeRetryableDetailsEveryStatus`). Exceptions without a server body keep today's classification.
393: - `SecretRedactor` (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Redaction`): `Redact(text)` and `ContainsSecret(text)` over the rules of `SessionLogSanitizer` and `ApiKeyRedaction` (`src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/SessionLogSanitizer.cs:15`, `src/QBrainAi.Common.AgentCli/ApiKeyRedaction.cs:9`). It is the one redactor behind the session-log sanitizer's review paths and the agent-context secret filter and secret scan (section 3, Secrets).
394: - `ContentHasher` (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Hashing`): SHA-256 over UTF-8 bytes, lower-case hex, of the text's stored normal form; every hash this plan names is computed through it. `McpDbContext` rewrites every string it saves through `LineSanitizer.Sanitize`, which replaces U+2014 and U+2013 with an ASCII hyphen (`McpDbContext.cs:1351-1360,1704-1718`, `src/QBrainAi.Common.AgentCli/LineSanitizer.cs:23-28`); ContentHasher applies the same function before hashing, and every byte-for-byte comparison of this plan (Replay identity, `verdict_binding`, `reviewer_turn`) compares normal forms, so a value read back from the store hashes and compares as it was recorded (`ContentHasherTextWithEmAndEnDashesStoredAndReadBackHashEqual`).

2661: ### 6.1 Scope and principles
2662: 
2663: - Each agent invocation can run stateless: it receives a bounded, reproducible context package instead of carrying conversation history forward. In `Stateless` the model's input is the rendered package, the current request, and the deterministic `REQUIRED MEMORIES` block the host already injects (FR-MCP-MEMORY-003, -007, which hold unchanged; section 3.1, "Memories in Stateless mode"); history stays excluded.
2664: - A package contains the current request, the canonical operator profile and standing rules, the applicable requirements, related session-log evidence, trusted prior responses, and relevant code at the current commit, each with its provenance.
2665: - The relational store is authoritative for packages, responses, grades, and relationships. Response artifacts are projected into GraphRAG for semantic retrieval, with a deterministic relational fallback that gives the same result whenever GraphRAG is disabled, uninitialized, or unavailable.
2666: - A response becomes trusted only when a deterministic evidence grade and an independent model grade both reach correctness and completeness of at least 98 percent with zero FAIL and zero UNKNOWN findings. The model grade is recorded by the HV agent for the responses of an HV request that names a range of session-log turns; this effort has no grading worker or HV pipeline (operator, 2026-10-11). Rejected, stale, and superseded responses are kept for audit and never retrieved as trusted context.
2667: - Mandatory context is never truncated: when it exceeds the token budget, package construction fails explicitly, and in `Pilot` or `Stateless` mode the invocation fails: no answer is produced (operator, 2026-10-11: "Fail the invocation").
2668: - The mode is opt-in (`Mcp:AgentContext:Mode`); the current stateful behavior stays the default during the pilot. In `Off` the agent-context commands are refused and every stored record stays readable for audit (section 6.2).
2669: - Requirement ids (reserved for Phase 1, the plan's P0 steps 1-9, and created there with acceptance criteria, mappings, and use cases): FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-001 package construction and provenance; -002 token budget and overflow; -003 response submission; -004 grading, HV requests, and trust; -005 rejection, staleness, and supersession; -006 typed relationships; -007 GraphRAG projection and fallback; -008 REST, MCP, client, REPL, and plugin surfaces; -009 opt-in mode and pilot. The matching TR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-* and TEST-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-* records are created in Phase 1.
2670: - Existing records and stores this phase meets (the reconciliation, section 3.1), each with its relationship; none changes behavior unless the bullet names an update:
2671:   - FR-SUPPORT-010 context pack (`ContextPack`, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Models/ContextPack.cs:3-16`, `POST /qbrainai/context/pack`, `src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/Controllers/ContextController.cs:164-165`): related and separate, no reuse and no supersede. It returns ranked context chunks for a query; a context package is a stored, hashed, replayable snapshot of one request's mandatory and ranked sources. The FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-001 record states the distinction as a glossary entry.
2672:   - FR-MCP-082 bounded execution context (`TodoExecutionService.GetExecutionContextAsync`, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/TodoExecutionService.cs:456`): related, not reused, cross-referenced from FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-001. It summarizes one TODO's requirements and recent turns for resuming work; a package cites the TODO, requirement, and turn records themselves, each with the source hash staleness needs, which a summary does not carry.
2673:   - The FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW queue (requests with resolved artifact links, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/HostileReviewService.cs:290`, executions, findings, and its server-owned worker): separate. An HV request of this phase is a turn range an external HV agent grades, because this effort builds no grading worker (section 3.1); only RecordModelGradeCommand, after its eight checks, records a model grade, so a hostile review result is never one. The worker's identity (agent `Astra`, model `gpt-6-astra`, effort `xhigh`, enforced at startup, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Options/HostileReviewWorkerOptions.cs:13,16,19,77-82`) and `ModelGrader:*` (section 6.2) are separate option sets, so neither constrains the other; FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003 is unchanged by this phase.
2674:   - `MemoryEdgeEntity` (TR-MCP-MEMORY-MODEL-002, `src/QBrainAi.Storage/Entities/MemoryEdgeEntity.cs:5-32`): strengthen. The separate link store is justified against it beside the other link stores (section 6.3, `AgentContextRelationshipEntity`).
2675:   - GraphRAG: reuse. Projection calls `IGraphRagService.IngestTextAsync` and `DeleteDocumentAsync` (`src/QBrainAi.GraphRag/Services/IGraphRagService.cs:35,46`) and retrieval reports develop's fallback reasons (`src/QBrainAi.GraphRag/Services/GraphRagService.cs:880-889`). The registered service refuses those mutations while required turn transactions are active (`TransactionGatedGraphRagService`, TR-MCP-TXN-001, `src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/Services/TransactionGatedGraphRagService.cs:68-74,89-93`); a projection save then records the row `Failed` with `LastError`, and a later pass retries it (section 6.3, projection row states).
2676:   - Handoff idempotency: reuse. IdempotentCreate keeps the rule of TR-HANDOFF-TODO-001 (`src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/TodoPayloadFingerprint.cs:10`: the same key with an equal fingerprint returns the stored record, any other input is a conflict), and `HandoffDbExceptions.IsCommitAmbiguous` keeps its meaning (section 3.5.2).
2677:   - FR-MCP-130 AC 3 ("Only CuriosityEngine may request GraphRAG/context admission") governs QuadBrain brain-slot output (its description), and `src/QBrainAi.GraphRag` holds no Curiosity check (git grep at `a8d3934b`); projecting a trusted agent response is no brain-slot admission (updates FR-MCP-130 AC 3's wording to brain-slot output).
2678:   - FR-MCP-103 federation: strengthen. AC 1 enumerates every mutable state domain, so `agent_context` joins `FederationStateAdapterRegistry.RequiredDomains` (`src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/FederationStateAdapters.cs:128-142`) as a local-only domain through the existing `LocalOnlyFederationStateAdapter` registration (`src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/FederationAdapters/FederationStateAdapterServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:23-37`) and `InferDomain` maps `/qbrainai/agent-context` to it (`src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/FederationProxyService.cs:440-469`): it is never queued during a hub outage (`CanQueueDomain`, `:332-338`) and never applied from hub fanout (`src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/FederationOperationApplyService.cs:32-39`). A LocalProxy still forwards these routes live to the hub (AC 2, `FederationProxyService.ProxyAsync`, `:78`), so (inference) the hub's server holds the records and reads the commit from its own checkout of the workspace path, and answers 409 `agent_context_commit_unavailable` when it has none.
2679:   - FR-MCP-WIKIEXPORT-003: strengthen. Each new `DbSet` gets an explicit dump policy in `WikiDumpTablePolicyRegistry.PolicyFor` (`src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/WikiDumpTablePolicyRegistry.cs:19-43`): `COPY-SANITIZE+HISTORY+INERT`, the policy of the HostileReview tables (`:35-36`), for every agent-context table except `AgentContextProjections`, which is `OMIT-LOCAL` (`:28`) because its rows name GraphRAG documents of the source workspace (inference: a copied row would point at a document the destination does not hold). The registry coverage test (`tests/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Tests/Services/WikiDumpG7OverlayTests.cs:56-71`) covers the new sets.
2680: 
2681: ### 6.2 Configuration: `AgentContextOptions`
2682: 
2683: Section `Mcp:AgentContext` (declared under `QBrainAi: AgentContext:` in `appsettings.yaml`, projected onto `Mcp:` by `CanonicalSectionProjectionProvider`), class `AgentContextOptions` in `src/QBrainAi.Services/AgentContext/AgentContextOptions.cs` (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.AgentContext`) with `SectionName = "Mcp:AgentContext"`, a `Validate()` method, and `ValidateOnStart()`.
2684: 
2685: - `Mode` (enum `AgentContextMode`: `Off`, `Pilot`, `Stateless`; default `Off`). `Off`: ModeGateBehavior (section 3.5.1) refuses every agent-context command except DecideAgentResponseTrustCommand (dispatched only by the grade units) with 409 `agent_context_disabled`; GetAgentContextStatusQuery and every read-only agent-context query stay available, so packages, responses, grades, relationships, HV requests, and the pilot report stay readable for audit; a requirement update or delete dispatches EvaluateStalenessCommand only while Mode is not `Off`. `Pilot`: packages are built and responses graded, but plugins keep the stateful conversation (no injection). `Stateless`: plugins inject the package beside the host's `REQUIRED MEMORIES` block and carry no history, on a host with an authoritative history-exclusion operation recorded in its P0.2 row; any other host treats `Stateless` as `Pilot` (section 6.6). Plugin reading of the mode (section 3.1, resolutions of round 5): the plugin reads `mode` through GetAgentContextStatusQuery at host session start (StartHostSession, or the first prompt on a host without a SessionStart event: cline, cline-v2, and opencode) and caches it for that host session as `agentContextMode` in its `turn-state.yaml` through `Update-TurnState` (section 3.4, plugin per-turn store); that read is the plugin's only agent-context read at host session start, and the query counts responses by effective status with one source read per distinct dependency and commit, so it answers within the SessionStart hook bound (section 6.4, GetAgentContextStatusQuery); a `mode` it cannot read, including a read that times out or misses the hook bound, or a value it does not know, is treated as `Off`; a 409 `agent_context_disabled` answer to a build or a submission caches `Off`, and the host session continues statefully (no refusal, no `canceled` close); a change away from `Off` takes effect at the next host session start. A host whose prompt hook cannot refuse a prompt, or that runs the prompt anyway after a hook timeout, crash, or `plugin_core_unavailable`, runs `Pilot` and `Stateless` as `Off` and records that as a feature-matrix limitation (P0.2 probe (j) records each host's refusal capability); a message absorbed into a running turn (`absorbed_mid_turn`) runs as `Pilot`.
2686: - `TokenBudget` (int, default 32000, must be 1024..1000000).
2687: - `BytesPerToken` (int, default 4, must be 1..16): the deterministic token estimate is `ceil(utf8ByteCount / BytesPerToken)` per item.
2688: - `Trust:Correctness`, `Trust:Completeness` (decimal in [0.98, 1], default 0.98, inclusive): the attached plan's minimum of 98 percent is a floor that configuration cannot lower; a value below 0.98 or above 1 fails startup validation (`AgentContextOptionsTrustBelow098FailsStartup`, `AgentContextOptionsTrustAt098And1Accepted`). RunDeterministicGradeCommand and RecordModelGradeCommand derive and stamp each grade's verdict through ScoreVerdict (section 3.5.4) with `max(configured, 0.98)`; DecideAgentResponseTrustCommand never reads a stored verdict: it re-derives the verdict of each latest grade from that grade's stored scores and finding counts through ScoreVerdict against `max(configured now, 0.98)`, so no stored verdict or earlier threshold below the floor can trust a response (`TrustStoredThresholdBelowFloorFloorApplied`) and a raised threshold demotes a `Trusted` response at its next trust decision (`TrustThresholdRaisedAfterGradeAppliedAtNextDecision`). The Phase B review thresholds (FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-007) stay configurable as approved.
2689: - `MaxCandidatesPerKind` (int, default 50, 1..1000) and `MaxPriorResponses` (int, default 10, 0..100): after filtering and ranking, each optional kind keeps at most `MaxCandidatesPerKind` candidates in rank order (`PriorResponse` at most `MaxPriorResponses`), and the rest are omitted with reason `below_candidate_limit`; mandatory items are never cut by these limits (`BuildCandidatesBeyondPerKindLimitOmittedBelowCandidateLimit`, `BuildMaxPriorResponsesZeroNoPriorResponseItem`).
2690: - `ProfileSources` (list of file globs resolved on the server host; default `~/.claude/profile/*.md` excluding `add-profile*.md`, the set the `/add-profile` skill reads) and `RuleSources` (list of workspace-relative paths; default `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`, secret values redacted through SecretRedactor). Profile and rules are mandatory: when no profile file or no rule file resolves, the build fails with 409 `agent_context_profile_unavailable` instead of building a package without them. A rule file outside version control (the default `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml`, regenerated at every server start) is a package item with its hash for provenance and never a staleness dependency (no `derived_from` link), so a server restart does not make responses stale (`BuildUntrackedRuleSourceNoDerivedFromLinkHashKeptOnItem`, `StalenessServerRestartRegeneratesMarkerTrustedResponseStaysTrusted`).
2691: - `ModelGrader:AgentName` (default `Codex`), `ModelGrader:RequiredModel` (default `gpt-6-astra`), `ModelGrader:RequiredEffort` (default `max`), `ModelGrader:ReceiptRoot` (workspace-relative, default `docs/receipts/hv`): a model grade from any other grader, or whose receipts are outside the receipt root or do not verify, is refused.
2692: - `HvRequest:MaxTurns` (int, default 200, 1..2000): the largest turn range one HV request may name.
2693: - `GraphRag:ProjectionEnabled` (bool, default true): false skips ingest only; removal of a projected document still runs while GraphRAG is enabled (section 6.3, projection row states). `GraphRag:UseForRetrieval` (bool, default true): BuildAgentContextPackageCommand retrieves its candidates with `preferGraphRag` equal to this value, recorded in `OptionsSnapshotJson`, and every candidate's ranking inputs, GraphRAG scores included, are part of `InputsSha256` through `RankingFeaturesJson`, so two builds that rank differently never share it (`BuildGraphRagScoreChangedSameSourcesDifferentInputsSha256`).
2694: - Validation failures (startup): an unknown `Mode`, `TokenBudget`, `BytesPerToken`, `HvRequest:MaxTurns`, thresholds outside their ranges, an empty `RuleSources`, an empty grader identity, or an empty `ModelGrader:ReceiptRoot`. These ranges are enforced at server start by `Validate()` with `ValidateOnStart()` and proven by its G2 cases; they are not a G5 (`ValidateConfig`) check, an exclusion TR-MCP-NUKE-004 states (section 8.4).
2695: 
2696: ### 6.3 Entities (namespace `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage.Entities.AgentContext`)
2697: 
2698: Every entity below is a new type in `src/QBrainAi.Storage/Entities/AgentContext/`, so its namespace follows the folder rule of section 3.5; develop's existing entities keep `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage.Entities`. Table names keep the `AgentContext` or `AgentResponse` prefix because the database has no namespace.
2699: 
2700: Common rules:
2701: 
2702: - Readable keys: string keys `[StringLength(128)]`, human-readable and derived from the records they belong to (formats per entity below), allocated by ReadableKeyAllocator (section 3.5.2, strategy `NextOrdinal`). A key is `<prefix><parentId><tail>` when that is at most 128 characters; otherwise the embedded parent id is shortened to its first `128 - length(prefix) - length(tail) - 13` characters followed by `-` and the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the full parent id, so keys stay readable, deterministic, and distinct for distinct parents. 2661: ### 6.1 Scope and principles
2662: 
2663: - Each agent invocation can run stateless: it receives a bounded, reproducible context package instead of carrying conversation history forward. In `Stateless` the model's input is the rendered package, the current request, and the deterministic `REQUIRED MEMORIES` block the host already injects (FR-MCP-MEMORY-003, -007, which hold unchanged; section 3.1, "Memories in Stateless mode"); history stays excluded.
2664: - A package contains the current request, the canonical operator profile and standing rules, the applicable requirements, related session-log evidence, trusted prior responses, and relevant code at the current commit, each with its provenance.
2665: - The relational store is authoritative for packages, responses, grades, and relationships. Response artifacts are projected into GraphRAG for semantic retrieval, with a deterministic relational fallback that gives the same result whenever GraphRAG is disabled, uninitialized, or unavailable.
2666: - A response becomes trusted only when a deterministic evidence grade and an independent model grade both reach correctness and completeness of at least 98 percent with zero FAIL and zero UNKNOWN findings. The model grade is recorded by the HV agent for the responses of an HV request that names a range of session-log turns; this effort has no grading worker or HV pipeline (operator, 2026-10-11). Rejected, stale, and superseded responses are kept for audit and never retrieved as trusted context.
2667: - Mandatory context is never truncated: when it exceeds the token budget, package construction fails explicitly, and in `Pilot` or `Stateless` mode the invocation fails: no answer is produced (operator, 2026-10-11: "Fail the invocation").
2668: - The mode is opt-in (`Mcp:AgentContext:Mode`); the current stateful behavior stays the default during the pilot. In `Off` the agent-context commands are refused and every stored record stays readable for audit (section 6.2).
