2700: Common rules:
2701: 
2702: - Readable keys: string keys `[StringLength(128)]`, human-readable and derived from the records they belong to (formats per entity below), allocated by ReadableKeyAllocator (section 3.5.2, strategy `NextOrdinal`). A key is `<prefix><parentId><tail>` when that is at most 128 characters; otherwise the embedded parent id is shortened to its first `128 - length(prefix) - length(tail) - 13` characters followed by `-` and the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the full parent id, so keys stay readable, deterministic, and distinct for distinct parents. The complete parent ids are always stored in their own root-id columns, which keep the live length of 256 (`SessionLogEntity.SessionId` and `SessionLogTurnEntity.RequestId` allow 256), so no root id is ever truncated (`ReadableKeyAllocatorMaxLengthRootIdsFitAndStayDistinct` on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server; `ReadableKeyAllocatorShortRootIdsKeepFullReadableForm`). The sequence suffix `<nn>` has at least two digits, starts at 01, is one more than the highest stored suffix for that prefix in the workspace compared as a number, and widens past 99 (100, 101, and so on) (`ReadableKeyAllocatorSuffixPast99WidensLatestGradeOrderKept`). A unique-index violation from a concurrent insert declares a retry to SerializableWrite with the next suffix; agent-context keys use SerializableWrite's default bound (four attempts), then 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` (only the Phase A minter states its own bound, for one cause, a collision of its random request id: six attempts and 500 `mint_collision_exhausted`; its transient conflicts keep the default bound and the 409 exit, section 3.1, "Retry bound", and section 4.2).
2703: - Keys are per workspace: every entity with a readable key has the composite primary key (`WorkspaceId`, `<key>`), the pattern develop uses so one TODO id can exist in several workspaces (TR-MCP-TODO-008, `src/QBrainAi.Storage/McpDbContext.cs:583-585`), and every reference to it is the composite foreign key (`WorkspaceId`, `<key>`). Every readable-key, idempotency-key, and natural unique index therefore includes `WorkspaceId`, and ReadableKeyAllocator reads its highest suffix in the workspace (under the `Workspace` query filter and past the soft-delete filter), so two workspaces that hold the same legacy request id get the same key string on two rows, without a collision and without exhausting the retries (`ReadableKeyAllocatorSameParentIdTwoWorkspacesSameKeyNoCollisionNoExhaustion`; request ids are unique only within a session, `McpDbContext.cs:391,404`).
2704: - Child rows use `long` identity keys; each references its parent through the composite foreign key (`WorkspaceId`, parent key), and every composite unique key of a child is (`WorkspaceId`, parent key, ...) (stated per entity). Because `WorkspaceId` is part of that foreign key, a child's `WorkspaceId` always equals its parent's; StorageSchema's `ResolveWorkspaceIdForAddedEntity` cases stamp it from the parent, as develop stamps session-log children (BUG-SESSIONLOG-WS-002, `McpDbContext.cs:1665-1669`).
2705: - Root ids (section 3.1, "Root ids"): every child row carries `WorkspaceId` and the root ids of every parent it hangs from, copied from the parent in the same transaction and never changed. The turn key is `Agent` (64), `SessionId` (256), and `RequestId` (256) together, because a request id is unique only within its session (sessions are unique by (`WorkspaceId`, `SourceType`, `SessionId`) and turns by (`SessionLogId`, `RequestId`), `McpDbContext.cs:391,404`). A package child (item, focus ref, input, input link, omission, finding) carries `PackageId` and the turn key; a response child (claim, evidence) and a projection row carry `ResponseId`, `PackageId`, and the turn key; a grade carries `ResponseId`, `PackageId`, the turn key, and, for a model grade, `HvRequestId`; a grade finding carries `GradeId` and every root id of its grade; an HV request item carries `HvRequestId`, `ResponseId`, `PackageId`, and the turn key. The root-id columns join no key or index beyond those stated per entity, because no unit reads a child by them (`RootIdsEveryAgentContextChildRowEqualsItsParents`, over every table of this section).
2706: - Every entity has `[Required][StringLength(1024)] WorkspaceId` with the named `Workspace` query filter and `StampWorkspaceId` on add; timestamps are `DateTimeOffset` named `*Utc`; decimals are `HasPrecision(29, 28)`; list-valued data is stored in 4NF child tables; every hash is SHA-256 over the UTF-8 bytes of the text's stored normal form in lower-case hex, computed through ContentHasher (section 3.5.2: `McpDbContext` replaces em and en dashes in every string it saves, and ContentHasher hashes that same form), so a value read back from the store hashes as it was recorded, and every byte-for-byte check of this phase (Replay identity, `ContentSha256`, `verdict_binding`, `reviewer_turn`) compares normal forms; every column described as sanitized is written through SecretRedactor (section 3.5.2). Agent-context records are redacted when written, so no secret value is stored in a package or a response, while session-log turns keep FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGSAN-001's outbound-only redaction (AC 2); SecretRedactor holds the one rule set for both.
2707: - Idempotency: a create that carries an idempotency key or a natural unique key runs IdempotentCreate (section 3.5.2) over that unique index with policy `Conflict`: the key is looked up first, before any precondition that can change between attempts, and the stored PayloadFingerprint of the client inputs (never of server-observed sources) is compared; an equal fingerprint returns the stored record, another is 409 `conflict` with `retryable: false`. A unit that reads outside the database before its SerializableWrite (Build, Submit, the two grades) runs the same lookup read-only before those reads, so a retry of a lost response returns the stored record without reading a source. RelationshipWriter uses policy `ReturnStored`. The store has no concurrency tokens.
2708: - Soft delete (TR-MCP-DB-003): `McpDbContext` turns every delete of these entities into a soft delete, hides deleted rows through its `SoftDelete` query filter, and its keys and unique indexes cover deleted rows (`McpDbContext.cs:391,404,1302-1338,1363-1380`). The revive rule of IdempotentCreate and ReadableKeyAllocator (section 3.5.2) acts on each key as follows. The relationship's six-field key: DeleteAgentContextRelationshipCommand is the one unit that deletes an agent-context row (a client-made link); creating the identical link again revives that row, keeps its `RelationshipId`, sets `ToSha256`, `EvidenceRef`, `CreatedBy`, and `CreatedUtc` from the new create, and returns `created: true` (`CreateRelationshipAfterDeleteRevivedSameRelationshipIdCreatedTrue`). The readable keys (`pkg-`, `rsp-`, `grd-`, `rel-`, `hvr-`): ReadableKeyAllocator counts deleted suffixes, so a deleted link's `rel-` suffix is never given to another link (`ReadableKeyAllocatorSoftDeletedSuffixNeverReused`). The idempotency keys of packages, responses, and HV requests, and the model grade's natural key: no unit or surface deletes these records or their child rows, because they are kept for audit (section 6.1), so in this design their lookups never meet a deleted row.
2709: - Write isolation: every unit that checks a response's status or grades, an HV request, or an idempotency or readable key and then saves runs its checks and its save as one delegate through SerializableWrite (section 3.5.2; the convention of `SessionLogService.cs:156`): BuildAgentContextPackageCommand, SubmitAgentResponseCommand, RunDeterministicGradeCommand and RecordModelGradeCommand with DecideAgentResponseTrustCommand, RejectAgentResponseCommand, SupersedeAgentResponseCommand, EvaluateStalenessCommand, CreateAgentContextRelationshipCommand, ProjectAgentResponsesCommand (each ProjectOneResponse save), and CreateAgentContextHvRequestCommand. Each delegate is database-only (section 3.1, "Database-only delegates"): the unit reads the git commit, files, sources and their hashes (each relationship target's `ToSha256` included), retrieval and GraphRAG results, git ancestry, and receipts before SerializableWrite, after its read-only idempotency lookup where it has a key, and its delegate re-checks the database state those reads relied on (each locked response's `StatusVersion`, the turn, the HV request); a changed state ends the attempt and the unit runs again from its reads, within the same bound. Build reads each prior response's staleness read-only and persists only its package with its child rows and its links; only EvaluateStalenessCommand persists `Stale` (through ResponseStatusTransition). A grade unit (RunDeterministicGradeCommand, RecordModelGradeCommand) runs every read-only check it has (the response, the HV request, the evidence and secret scan of a deterministic grade, the receipt, reviewer, and runtime-identity checks of a model grade), then dispatches EvaluateStalenessCommand for its response, then runs its own SerializableWrite, whose delegate re-checks the response's `StatusVersion` and dispatches DecideAgentResponseTrustCommand, which reads only the database (the status that dispatch left and the stored grades) and persists no `Stale`. Per-response writes name their responses, and the transaction's first statements increment each named response's `StatusVersion` in ascending `ResponseId` order (a supersede names the original and the replacement, an HV request every candidate response before it re-reads their status and inserts the items, a projection save its response), so every such operation on one response takes the row's write lock first and they serialize in commit order on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server. A transient conflict (`DbErrorClassifier.IsTransientConflict`: PostgreSQL 40001 or 40P01, SQL Server 1205, SQLite 5 busy or 6 locked) or a unique violation on a key the unit declares rolls the whole delegate back and runs it again, at most three times (four attempts, SerializableWrite's default bound); then the unit returns 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` and saves nothing (`TrustForcedInterleavingDeterministicFailVsModelPassNeverTrustedOnSupersededGrade`, `TrustForcedInterleavingRejectVsGradeRejectedNeverRevived`, `HvRequestForcedCreateVsRejectNoPendingItemOnTerminalResponse`, `HvRequestForcedCreateVsSupersedeNoPendingItemOnTerminalResponse`, `HvRequestForcedConcurrentOverlappingCreatesEachResponsePendingInAtMostOneOpenRequest`, `LifecycleForcedInterleavingSupersedeVsRejectSameOriginalOneWinsOtherRefused`, each on the three providers).

2661: ### 6.1 Scope and principles
2662: 
2663: - Each agent invocation can run stateless: it receives a bounded, reproducible context package instead of carrying conversation history forward. In `Stateless` the model's input is the rendered package, the current request, and the deterministic `REQUIRED MEMORIES` block the host already injects (FR-MCP-MEMORY-003, -007, which hold unchanged; section 3.1, "Memories in Stateless mode"); history stays excluded.
2664: - A package contains the current request, the canonical operator profile and standing rules, the applicable requirements, related session-log evidence, trusted prior responses, and relevant code at the current commit, each with its provenance.
2665: - The relational store is authoritative for packages, responses, grades, and relationships. Response artifacts are projected into GraphRAG for semantic retrieval, with a deterministic relational fallback that gives the same result whenever GraphRAG is disabled, uninitialized, or unavailable.
2666: - A response becomes trusted only when a deterministic evidence grade and an independent model grade both reach correctness and completeness of at least 98 percent with zero FAIL and zero UNKNOWN findings. The model grade is recorded by the HV agent for the responses of an HV request that names a range of session-log turns; this effort has no grading worker or HV pipeline (operator, 2026-10-11). Rejected, stale, and superseded responses are kept for audit and never retrieved as trusted context.
2667: - Mandatory context is never truncated: when it exceeds the token budget, package construction fails explicitly, and in `Pilot` or `Stateless` mode the invocation fails: no answer is produced (operator, 2026-10-11: "Fail the invocation").
2668: - The mode is opt-in (`Mcp:AgentContext:Mode`); the current stateful behavior stays the default during the pilot. In `Off` the agent-context commands are refused and every stored record stays readable for audit (section 6.2).
2669: - Requirement ids (reserved for Phase 1, the plan's P0 steps 1-9, and created there with acceptance criteria, mappings, and use cases): FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-001 package construction and provenance; -002 token budget and overflow; -003 response submission; -004 grading, HV requests, and trust; -005 rejection, staleness, and supersession; -006 typed relationships; -007 GraphRAG projection and fallback; -008 REST, MCP, client, REPL, and plugin surfaces; -009 opt-in mode and pilot. The matching TR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-* and TEST-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-* records are created in Phase 1.
2670: - Existing records and stores this phase meets (the reconciliation, section 3.1), each with its relationship; none changes behavior unless the bullet names an update:
2671:   - FR-SUPPORT-010 context pack (`ContextPack`, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Models/ContextPack.cs:3-16`, `POST /qbrainai/context/pack`, `src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/Controllers/ContextController.cs:164-165`): related and separate, no reuse and no supersede. It returns ranked context chunks for a query; a context package is a stored, hashed, replayable snapshot of one request's mandatory and ranked sources. The FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-001 record states the distinction as a glossary entry.
2672:   - FR-MCP-082 bounded execution context (`TodoExecutionService.GetExecutionContextAsync`, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/TodoExecutionService.cs:456`): related, not reused, cross-referenced from FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-001. It summarizes one TODO's requirements and recent turns for resuming work; a package cites the TODO, requirement, and turn records themselves, each with the source hash staleness needs, which a summary does not carry.
2673:   - The FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW queue (requests with resolved artifact links, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/HostileReviewService.cs:290`, executions, findings, and its server-owned worker): separate. An HV request of this phase is a turn range an external HV agent grades, because this effort builds no grading worker (section 3.1); only RecordModelGradeCommand, after its eight checks, records a model grade, so a hostile review result is never one. The worker's identity (agent `Astra`, model `gpt-6-astra`, effort `xhigh`, enforced at startup, `src/QBrainAi.Services/Options/HostileReviewWorkerOptions.cs:13,16,19,77-82`) and `ModelGrader:*` (section 6.2) are separate option sets, so neither constrains the other; FR-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003 is unchanged by this phase.
2674:   - `MemoryEdgeEntity` (TR-MCP-MEMORY-MODEL-002, `src/QBrainAi.Storage/Entities/MemoryEdgeEntity.cs:5-32`): strengthen. The separate link store is justified against it beside the other link stores (section 6.3, `AgentContextRelationshipEntity`).
2675:   - GraphRAG: reuse. Projection calls `IGraphRagService.IngestTextAsync` and `DeleteDocumentAsync` (`src/QBrainAi.GraphRag/Services/IGraphRagService.cs:35,46`) and retrieval reports develop's fallback reasons (`src/QBrainAi.GraphRag/Services/GraphRagService.cs:880-889`). The registered service refuses those mutations while required turn transactions are active (`TransactionGatedGraphRagService`, TR-MCP-TXN-001, `src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/Services/TransactionGatedGraphRagService.cs:68-74,89-93`); a projection save then records the row `Failed` with `LastError`, and a later pass retries it (section 6.3, projection row states).
2676:   - Handoff idempotency: reuse. 2661: ### 6.1 Scope and principles
2662: 
2663: - Each agent invocation can run stateless: it receives a bounded, reproducible context package instead of carrying conversation history forward. 2698: Every entity below is a new type in `src/QBrainAi.Storage/Entities/AgentContext/`, so its namespace follows the folder rule of section 3.5; develop's existing entities keep `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Storage.Entities`. 2700: Common rules:
2701: 
2702: - Readable keys: string keys `[StringLength(128)]`, human-readable and derived from the records they belong to (formats per entity below), allocated by ReadableKeyAllocator (section 3.5.2, strategy `NextOrdinal`). A key is `<prefix><parentId><tail>` when that is at most 128 characters; otherwise the embedded parent id is shortened to its first `128 - length(prefix) - length(tail) - 13` characters followed by `-` and the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the full parent id, so keys stay readable, deterministic, and distinct for distinct parents. The complete parent ids are always stored in their own root-id columns, which keep the live length of 256 (`SessionLogEntity.SessionId` and `SessionLogTurnEntity.RequestId` allow 256), so no root id is ever truncated (`ReadableKeyAllocatorMaxLengthRootIdsFitAndStayDistinct` on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server; `ReadableKeyAllocatorShortRootIdsKeepFullReadableForm`). The sequence suffix `<nn>` has at least two digits, starts at 01, is one more than the highest stored suffix for that prefix in the workspace compared as a number, and widens past 99 (100, 101, and so on) (`ReadableKeyAllocatorSuffixPast99WidensLatestGradeOrderKept`). A unique-index violation from a concurrent insert declares a retry to SerializableWrite with the next suffix; agent-context keys use SerializableWrite's default bound (four attempts), then 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` (only the Phase A minter states its own bound, for one cause, a collision of its random request id: six attempts and 500 `mint_collision_exhausted`; its transient conflicts keep the default bound and the 409 exit, section 3.1, "Retry bound", and section 4.2).
2703: - Keys are per workspace: every entity with a readable key has the composite primary key (`WorkspaceId`, `<key>`), the pattern develop uses so one TODO id can exist in several workspaces (TR-MCP-TODO-008, `src/QBrainAi.Storage/McpDbContext.cs:583-585`), and every reference to it is the composite foreign key (`WorkspaceId`, `<key>`). Every readable-key, idempotency-key, and natural unique index therefore includes `WorkspaceId`, and ReadableKeyAllocator reads its highest suffix in the workspace (under the `Workspace` query filter and past the soft-delete filter), so two workspaces that hold the same legacy request id get the same key string on two rows, without a collision and without exhausting the retries (`ReadableKeyAllocatorSameParentIdTwoWorkspacesSameKeyNoCollisionNoExhaustion`; request ids are unique only within a session, `McpDbContext.cs:391,404`).
2704: - Child rows use `long` identity keys; each references its parent through the composite foreign key (`WorkspaceId`, parent key), and every composite unique key of a child is (`WorkspaceId`, parent key, ...) (stated per entity). Because `WorkspaceId` is part of that foreign key, a child's `WorkspaceId` always equals its parent's; StorageSchema's `ResolveWorkspaceIdForAddedEntity` cases stamp it from the parent, as develop stamps session-log children (BUG-SESSIONLOG-WS-002, `McpDbContext.cs:1665-1669`).
2705: - Root ids (section 3.1, "Root ids"): every child row carries `WorkspaceId` and the root ids of every parent it hangs from, copied from the parent in the same transaction and never changed. The turn key is `Agent` (64), `SessionId` (256), and `RequestId` (256) together, because a request id is unique only within its session (sessions are unique by (`WorkspaceId`, `SourceType`, `SessionId`) and turns by (`SessionLogId`, `RequestId`), `McpDbContext.cs:391,404`). A package child (item, focus ref, input, input link, omission, finding) carries `PackageId` and the turn key; a response child (claim, evidence) and a projection row carry `ResponseId`, `PackageId`, and the turn key; a grade carries `ResponseId`, `PackageId`, the turn key, and, for a model grade, `HvRequestId`; a grade finding carries `GradeId` and every root id of its grade; an HV request item carries `HvRequestId`, `ResponseId`, `PackageId`, and the turn key. The root-id columns join no key or index beyond those stated per entity, because no unit reads a child by them (`RootIdsEveryAgentContextChildRowEqualsItsParents`, over every table of this section).
2706: - Every entity has `[Required][StringLength(1024)] WorkspaceId` with the named `Workspace` query filter and `StampWorkspaceId` on add; timestamps are `DateTimeOffset` named `*Utc`; decimals are `HasPrecision(29, 28)`; list-valued data is stored in 4NF child tables; every hash is SHA-256 over the UTF-8 bytes of the text's stored normal form in lower-case hex, computed through ContentHasher (section 3.5.2: `McpDbContext` replaces em and en dashes in every string it saves, and ContentHasher hashes that same form), so a value read back from the store hashes as it was recorded, and every byte-for-byte check of this phase (Replay identity, `ContentSha256`, `verdict_binding`, `reviewer_turn`) compares normal forms; every column described as sanitized is written through SecretRedactor (section 3.5.2). Agent-context records are redacted when written, so no secret value is stored in a package or a response, while session-log turns keep FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGSAN-001's outbound-only redaction (AC 2); SecretRedactor holds the one rule set for both.
2707: - Idempotency: a create that carries an idempotency key or a natural unique key runs IdempotentCreate (section 3.5.2) over that unique index with policy `Conflict`: the key is looked up first, before any precondition that can change between attempts, and the stored PayloadFingerprint of the client inputs (never of server-observed sources) is compared; an equal fingerprint returns the stored record, another is 409 `conflict` with `retryable: false`. A unit that reads outside the database before its SerializableWrite (Build, Submit, the two grades) runs the same lookup read-only before those reads, so a retry of a lost response returns the stored record without reading a source. RelationshipWriter uses policy `ReturnStored`. The store has no concurrency tokens.
2708: - Soft delete (TR-MCP-DB-003): `McpDbContext` turns every delete of these entities into a soft delete, hides deleted rows through its `SoftDelete` query filter, and its keys and unique indexes cover deleted rows (`McpDbContext.cs:391,404,1302-1338,1363-1380`). The revive rule of IdempotentCreate and ReadableKeyAllocator (section 3.5.2) acts on each key as follows. The relationship's six-field key: DeleteAgentContextRelationshipCommand is the one unit that deletes an agent-context row (a client-made link); creating the identical link again revives that row, keeps its `RelationshipId`, sets `ToSha256`, `EvidenceRef`, `CreatedBy`, and `CreatedUtc` from the new create, and returns `created: true` (`CreateRelationshipAfterDeleteRevivedSameRelationshipIdCreatedTrue`). The readable keys (`pkg-`, `rsp-`, `grd-`, `rel-`, `hvr-`): ReadableKeyAllocator counts deleted suffixes, so a deleted link's `rel-` suffix is never given to another link (`ReadableKeyAllocatorSoftDeletedSuffixNeverReused`). The idempotency keys of packages, responses, and HV requests, and the model grade's natural key: no unit or surface deletes these records or their child rows, because they are kept for audit (section 6.1), so in this design their lookups never meet a deleted row.
2709: - Write isolation: every unit that checks a response's status or grades, an HV request, or an idempotency or readable key and then saves runs its checks and its save as one delegate through SerializableWrite (section 3.5.2; the convention of `SessionLogService.cs:156`): BuildAgentContextPackageCommand, SubmitAgentResponseCommand, RunDeterministicGradeCommand and RecordModelGradeCommand with DecideAgentResponseTrustCommand, RejectAgentResponseCommand, SupersedeAgentResponseCommand, EvaluateStalenessCommand, CreateAgentContextRelationshipCommand, ProjectAgentResponsesCommand (each ProjectOneResponse save), and CreateAgentContextHvRequestCommand. Each delegate is database-only (section 3.1, "Database-only delegates"): the unit reads the git commit, files, sources and their hashes (each relationship target's `ToSha256` included), retrieval and GraphRAG results, git ancestry, and receipts before SerializableWrite, after its read-only idempotency lookup where it has a key, and its delegate re-checks the database state those reads relied on (each locked response's `StatusVersion`, the turn, the HV request); a changed state ends the attempt and the unit runs again from its reads, within the same bound. Build reads each prior response's staleness read-only and persists only its package with its child rows and its links; only EvaluateStalenessCommand persists `Stale` (through ResponseStatusTransition). A grade unit (RunDeterministicGradeCommand, RecordModelGradeCommand) runs every read-only check it has (the response, the HV request, the evidence and secret scan of a deterministic grade, the receipt, reviewer, and runtime-identity checks of a model grade), then dispatches EvaluateStalenessCommand for its response, then runs its own SerializableWrite, whose delegate re-checks the response's `StatusVersion` and dispatches DecideAgentResponseTrustCommand, which reads only the database (the status that dispatch left and the stored grades) and persists no `Stale`. Per-response writes name their responses, and the transaction's first statements increment each named response's `StatusVersion` in ascending `ResponseId` order (a supersede names the original and the replacement, an HV request every candidate response before it re-reads their status and inserts the items, a projection save its response), so every such operation on one response takes the row's write lock first and they serialize in commit order on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server. A transient conflict (`DbErrorClassifier.IsTransientConflict`: PostgreSQL 40001 or 40P01, SQL Server 1205, SQLite 5 busy or 6 locked) or a unique violation on a key the unit declares rolls the whole delegate back and runs it again, at most three times (four attempts, SerializableWrite's default bound); then the unit returns 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` and saves nothing (`TrustForcedInterleavingDeterministicFailVsModelPassNeverTrustedOnSupersededGrade`, `TrustForcedInterleavingRejectVsGradeRejectedNeverRevived`, `HvRequestForcedCreateVsRejectNoPendingItemOnTerminalResponse`, `HvRequestForcedCreateVsSupersedeNoPendingItemOnTerminalResponse`, `HvRequestForcedConcurrentOverlappingCreatesEachResponsePendingInAtMostOneOpenRequest`, `LifecycleForcedInterleavingSupersedeVsRejectSameOriginalOneWinsOtherRefused`, each on the three providers).

2839: 4. `verdict_binding`: that verdict names this `hvRequestId` and has a `grades` entry for this `responseId` whose `contentSha256` equals the response's `ContentSha256` (both over the stored normal form of the content the reviewer read from the server).
2840: 5. `verdict_match`: the submitted `correctness`, `completeness`, and `findings` equal that entry exactly (the same score lexemes, compared as ScoreLexeme values that no hop re-serializes, section 3.5.4; the same claimIds, checks, and outcomes in the same order), and the entry's findings name every claim of the response at least once (an empty or partial finding list is refused). 2848: 
2849: - `WorkspaceId`, `ResponseId`, and the response's root ids `PackageId` (128), `Agent` (64), `SessionId` (256), `RequestId` (256).
2850: - `State` (16): `Pending`, `Projected`, `Removed`, `Skipped`, `Failed`, changed only by ResponseStatusTransition (section 3.5.5) and by a ProjectOneResponse save, as the projection row state diagram below draws. The row is created `Pending` when its response first enters `Trusted`.
2851: - `GraphRagDocumentId` (128): the document while one exists in GraphRAG (kept on a `Failed` row after a delete error and on a `Pending` row awaiting removal), `ProjectedContentSha256` (64), `LastError` (2048), `UpdatedUtc`.
2852: - Selection: a projection pass without `responseIds` selects `Pending` and `Failed` rows, and `Skipped` rows while ingest is enabled again; named `responseIds` select their rows in any state.
2853: - Lifecycle rules: for a response that is not `Trusted`, a row that holds a `GraphRagDocumentId` has its document deleted on the next pass while GraphRAG is enabled, whatever `ProjectionEnabled` says (`ProjectionDeleteFailedRetriedNextPassDocumentRemoved`, `ProjectionDisabledAfterProjectedRejectedResponseDocumentStillRemoved`); a selected row whose response is not `Trusted` and that holds no document becomes `Removed` and is not selected again (`ProjectionPendingThenRejectedBeforeIngestRowRemovedNotReselected`); `ProjectionEnabled` false skips ingest only (`Skipped`, `skippedReason` `projection_disabled`); while GraphRAG is disabled an ingest is `Skipped` (`skippedReason` `graphrag_disabled`) and a row awaiting removal stays `Pending` until GraphRAG is enabled (`ProjectionGraphRagDisabledRemovalStaysPendingRunsWhenEnabled`). ProjectOneResponse makes its GraphRAG call before SerializableWrite (database-only delegate), then saves the row through SerializableWrite with its response locked and re-reads the response status inside the delegate, so a reject that commits during an ingest leaves the row `Pending` with the new document id, removed on the next pass (`ProjectionForcedInterleavingRejectDuringIngestDocumentRemovedNextPass`, on the three providers); the delegate also re-reads the row, and a save that finds it already `Projected` by an overlapping pass for the same content keeps that document and deletes its own after the save (`ProjectionOverlappingPassesOneDocumentKeptOtherDeleted`). Every pass ends with ReconcileProjectedDocuments (section 6.5): an `agent-response` document of the workspace that no `Projected` row names and that was ingested before the pass started is deleted, and a `Projected` row whose document is gone returns to `Pending`, so racing ingests, a save that exhausted its retries after an ingest, and a failed delete leave no document past the next complete pass.
2854: - Workspace scope: projection ingests only into `GraphRagStorageScope.Workspace`, the GraphRAG retrieval path queries only that scope, and a hit naming a response outside the workspace is dropped, so a projected document never reaches the global GraphRAG scope or another workspace (`ProjectionAndGraphRagRetrievalWorkspaceScopedNoCrossWorkspaceHit`).

2835: 
2836: 1. `receipt_path`: both jsonl paths resolve inside the workspace under `ModelGrader:ReceiptRoot`.
2837: 2. `request_meta`: the request jsonl's first line is a JSON object with `type` `hv_request_meta` whose `reviewer.agent` contains `ModelGrader:AgentName`, `reviewer.model` equals `ModelGrader:RequiredModel`, and `reviewer.effort` equals `ModelGrader:RequiredEffort` (the HV runner writes exactly this object), and the request jsonl's body record names the `hvRequestId`.
2838: 3. `verdict_block`: the response jsonl records a completed turn (`turn.completed`) whose last agent message contains exactly one `=== VERDICT JSON ===` block that parses as one JSON object.

2851: - `GraphRagDocumentId` (128): the document while one exists in GraphRAG (kept on a `Failed` row after a delete error and on a `Pending` row awaiting removal), `ProjectedContentSha256` (64), `LastError` (2048), `UpdatedUtc`.
2852: - Selection: a projection pass without `responseIds` selects `Pending` and `Failed` rows, and `Skipped` rows while ingest is enabled again; named `responseIds` select their rows in any state.
2853: - Lifecycle rules: for a response that is not `Trusted`, a row that holds a `GraphRagDocumentId` has its document deleted on the next pass while GraphRAG is enabled, whatever `ProjectionEnabled` says (`ProjectionDeleteFailedRetriedNextPassDocumentRemoved`, `ProjectionDisabledAfterProjectedRejectedResponseDocumentStillRemoved`); a selected row whose response is not `Trusted` and that holds no document becomes `Removed` and is not selected again (`ProjectionPendingThenRejectedBeforeIngestRowRemovedNotReselected`); `ProjectionEnabled` false skips ingest only (`Skipped`, `skippedReason` `projection_disabled`); while GraphRAG is disabled an ingest is `Skipped` (`skippedReason` `graphrag_disabled`) and a row awaiting removal stays `Pending` until GraphRAG is enabled (`ProjectionGraphRagDisabledRemovalStaysPendingRunsWhenEnabled`). ProjectOneResponse makes its GraphRAG call before SerializableWrite (database-only delegate), then saves the row through SerializableWrite with its response locked and re-reads the response status inside the delegate, so a reject that commits during an ingest leaves the row `Pending` with the new document id, removed on the next pass (`ProjectionForcedInterleavingRejectDuringIngestDocumentRemovedNextPass`, on the three providers); the delegate also re-reads the row, and a save that finds it already `Projected` by an overlapping pass for the same content keeps that document and deletes its own after the save (`ProjectionOverlappingPassesOneDocumentKeptOtherDeleted`). Every pass ends with ReconcileProjectedDocuments (section 6.5): an `agent-response` document of the workspace that no `Projected` row names and that was ingested before the pass started is deleted, and a `Projected` row whose document is gone returns to `Pending`, so racing ingests, a save that exhausted its retries after an ingest, and a failed delete leave no document past the next complete pass.

Response 201 `AgentContextPackageResult` with status `Built` (Location `/qbrainai/agent-context/packages/{packageId}`), or 200 with the stored `Built` package when the idempotency key repeats with identical client inputs. 177: Resolutions of the plan derivation (coordinator readings of 2026-10-13 for questions the domain plan editors raised; each reuses an existing mechanism):
178: 
179: - Requirement writes and staleness: `RequirementsDatabaseDocumentService`, the database implementation of `IRequirementsDocumentService` (`src/QBrainAi.Services/Requirements/IRequirementsDocumentService.cs:9`), dispatches EvaluateStalenessCommand after the commit of each write that changes or deletes a requirement record or its acceptance criteria (single writes, `UpdateBatchAsync`, `RequirementsDatabaseDocumentService.cs:817`, and the recovery apply and import that write through it), with the `responseIds` of the responses that cite a changed requirement (evidence `Ref`, or a `depends_on`, `derived_from`, or `supports` link to it); a change of the workspace's current requirement layer (`SetWorkspaceCurrentRequirementLayerAsync`, `:343`) dispatches it with no `responseIds`. The dispatch runs outside the requirement transaction and only while Mode is not `Off`; a dispatch that fails or exhausts its retries is logged and never fails the requirement write, because every read evaluates freshness itself. 634: - Response `SessionLogMintTurnResult`: `requestId` (`req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<8 hex>`), `outcome` (`created` or `merged`), and `storedStatus` on `merged` only (TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004 AC-005).
635:   - 201 `{ requestId, outcome: "created" }`: a new in-progress turn.
636:   - 200 `{ requestId, outcome: "merged", storedStatus }`: the same nonce was already minted in this MCP session; the same `requestId` is returned and a terminal turn is not reopened.
637: - Idempotency: the nonce lookup and the insert are IdempotentCreate keyed by (session, ingressNonce) with policy `ReturnStored`, inside SerializableWrite (section 3.5.2). The mint is one host event, so a repeated nonce returns the stored turn whatever the payload; no payload fingerprint is compared, because the nonce already identifies the event (the host's per-message id, or a SHA-256 of the event fields, section 3.2). A concurrent mint of the same nonce loses on the nonce index, and the rerun lookup returns the winner as `merged`. Request-id collisions use the minter's own bound (six attempts in all, then 500); transient conflicts use SerializableWrite's default bound (four attempts, then 409). The mint writes one turn under turn-level isolation (storage rules above).

634: - Response `SessionLogMintTurnResult`: `requestId` (`req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<8 hex>`), `outcome` (`created` or `merged`), and `storedStatus` on `merged` only (TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004 AC-005).
635:   - 201 `{ requestId, outcome: "created" }`: a new in-progress turn.
636:   - 200 `{ requestId, outcome: "merged", storedStatus }`: the same nonce was already minted in this MCP session; the same `requestId` is returned and a terminal turn is not reopened.
637: - Idempotency: the nonce lookup and the insert are IdempotentCreate keyed by (session, ingressNonce) with policy `ReturnStored`, inside SerializableWrite (section 3.5.2). The mint is one host event, so a repeated nonce returns the stored turn whatever the payload; no payload fingerprint is compared, because the nonce already identifies the event (the host's per-message id, or a SHA-256 of the event fields, section 3.2). A concurrent mint of the same nonce loses on the nonce index, and the rerun lookup returns the winner as `merged`. Request-id collisions use the minter's own bound (six attempts in all, then 500); transient conflicts use SerializableWrite's default bound (four attempts, then 409). The mint writes one turn under turn-level isolation (storage rules above).
638: - Errors: 400 `ingress_nonce_invalid` (missing or invalid nonce, TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004 AC-005), 400 `validation_error` (an invalid session id, TurnLocator `InvalidIdentifier`, or an invalid `planFile` or `todoId`), 404 with detail code `session_not_open` (TurnLocator `SessionNotFound`), 500 with final detail code `mint_collision_exhausted` after six request-id attempts, 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` after SerializableWrite's four attempts (nothing saved; a retryable answer, so the plugin keeps its failsafe mint record for the drain as for an outage, section 3.1).

In `Pilot` or `Stateless`, a delivered request continues with process RunStatelessInvocation (section 6.6), where a pending mint fails the invocation (section 3.1).

The hook takes `turn-open.lock` once and never waits: on contention it reports `turn-open-contended`, writes a failsafe diagnostic naming the prompt (as for `nonce_source_missing`), and mints nothing, and the Stop gate warns `turn-open-contended` naming the prompt (section 3.1). `Invoke-SessionOpen` and `Set-SessionUnsupported` called inside the open record into its one atomic replace instead of taking the lock again.
1023: - Write-ahead (TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001 AC-002): under the lock the hook applies the equal-field rule, then writes the failsafe mint record (nonce, binding, root-id envelope) before the first mint call. A created, merged, or merged-terminal result, and an equal-field fail-close, clear it after the replace; an outage or a retryable answer (a transport outage, 503 `backend_unavailable`, a busy store's 503 `persistence_error`, or 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true`) keeps it for process DrainFailsafe, which opens the session before it mints; a final refusal counts as the record's first final answer (`drainAttempts` 1), so the drain mints it again under the attempt budget, each drained final answer counting one more attempt (`Resolve-MintOutcome`, section 3.5.6), and then quarantines it (process DrainFailsafe), and the Stop gate warns naming the prompt while the record is queued or quarantined. A hook killed after that write ends at the next hook, verb, or SessionStart drain with exactly one server turn for the message, delivered once (section 3.1).

The first-ingress writer applies on a host without a SessionStart event when no `mcpSessionId` is recorded for the host session. The mint record follows the write-ahead rule above (`Resolve-MintOutcome`, section 3.5.6): a created, merged, or merged-terminal result and the equal-field fail-close clear it; an outage or a retryable answer keeps it for the drain; a final refusal keeps it with `drainAttempts` 1, so the drain mints it again under the attempt budget and then quarantines it (`PromptHookFinalMintRefusalRecordKeptDrainAttemptsOne`). 1022: - Lock: the open is one `Update-TurnState` change. The hook takes `turn-open.lock` once and never waits: on contention it reports `turn-open-contended`, writes a failsafe diagnostic naming the prompt (as for `nonce_source_missing`), and mints nothing, and the Stop gate warns `turn-open-contended` naming the prompt (section 3.1). `Invoke-SessionOpen` and `Set-SessionUnsupported` called inside the open record into its one atomic replace instead of taking the lock again.
1023: - Write-ahead (TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001 AC-002): under the lock the hook applies the equal-field rule, then writes the failsafe mint record (nonce, binding, root-id envelope) before the first mint call. A created, merged, or merged-terminal result, and an equal-field fail-close, clear it after the replace; an outage or a retryable answer (a transport outage, 503 `backend_unavailable`, a busy store's 503 `persistence_error`, or 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true`) keeps it for process DrainFailsafe, which opens the session before it mints; a final refusal counts as the record's first final answer (`drainAttempts` 1), so the drain mints it again under the attempt budget, each drained final answer counting one more attempt (`Resolve-MintOutcome`, section 3.5.6), and then quarantines it (process DrainFailsafe), and the Stop gate warns naming the prompt while the record is queued or quarantined. A hook killed after that write ends at the next hook, verb, or SessionStart drain with exactly one server turn for the message, delivered once (section 3.1).
1024: - First-ingress writer (hosts without a SessionStart event: classic cline, cline-v2, opencode): records a new `mcpSessionId` for the host session key only when none is recorded, in the open's replace, then opens it through `Invoke-SessionOpen` (section 3.4). From Phase C it is also the host session's Mode reader, as StartHostSession is on the other hosts: it reads the Mode with GetAgentContextStatusQuery at this first prompt and records `agentContextMode` in the same replace, `Off` when it cannot read it or does not know the value (section 3.4; section 3.1, "Mode changes").
1025: - Before the open, the hook drains its host session's failsafe when it holds drainable records (process DrainFailsafe), so an earlier prompt's mint reaches the server first.

The write-ahead mint record carries the nonce, the binding, and the root-id envelope. The first-ingress writer applies on a host without a SessionStart event when no `mcpSessionId` is recorded for the host session. A created turn is delivered (write target, `openDelivered`, ledger entry); a merged terminal turn reports its `storedStatus` and is never the write target, in the open list, or in the ledger. The mint record follows the write-ahead rule above (`Resolve-MintOutcome`, section 3.5.6): a created, merged, or merged-terminal result and the equal-field fail-close clear it; an outage or a retryable answer keeps it for the drain; a final refusal keeps it with `drainAttempts` 1, so the drain mints it again under the attempt budget and then quarantines it (`PromptHookFinalMintRefusalRecordKeptDrainAttemptsOne`). The first-ingress writer records the new `mcpSessionId` in this replace before `Invoke-SessionOpen` runs, so an open that meets an outage keeps that identity and the drain opens the same id (`TsHostFirstIngressOpenOutageRecordedSessionIdReusedByDrainNoSecondId`).

622: - Database-only delegates: no Phase A unit reads git, files, or sources. The turn context and workspace attribution checks are path string checks against the workspace root (`SessionLogWorkspaceAttributionValidator.cs:56-105` at `a8d3934b`), so each unit runs every check inside its SerializableWrite delegate and reads nothing before it.
623: - Isolation (section 3.1, "Turn-level isolation"): the mint and the single-turn writes (upsert, patch, replace, complete, fail) read their session row only to locate the parent and write only the one turn with its children (section 3.5.2, isolation scope), so writes to different turns of one session never answer a conflict (`TurnWriteConcurrentDifferentTurnsSameSessionBothCommitNoConflictAnswer`, dense-session fixture, three providers); the session summary refresh after a single-turn write is its own short write after the turn commits, and its failure never fails the turn write. SubmitSessionLogCommand keeps its session-level Serializable transaction, as `SessionLogService.SubmitAsync` does today (`SessionLogService.cs:155-157`). The mint inserts one turn and is a single-turn write like the others (section 3.1, "Mint isolation").
624: - Retry bound: SerializableWrite runs a delegate at most four attempts, then answers 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` and saves nothing; the attempts run within the unit's storage budget (FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-003). Only the minter states its own bound, for one cause, a collision of its random request id (six attempts, then 500 `mint_collision_exhausted`); its transient conflicts keep the default bound and the 409 `conflict` exit (section 3.1, "Retry bound").

A caller-owned EF or `System.Transactions` transaction is refused before any write, as develop's `SubmitAsync` refuses it (`SessionLogService.cs:119-128`); `SessionLogSupersessionTests.SubmitAsyncCallerTransactionRejectsBeforeMutation`, `SubmitAsyncAmbientTransactionRejectsBeforeMutation`, and `SubmitAsyncPendingTrackedEditRejectsWithoutDiscardingEdit` (`SessionLogSupersessionTests.cs:192,204,178` at `a8d3934b`, renamed on the analyzer branch) and `SessionLogControllerReceiptTests.SubmitAsyncOuterRollbackNeverReturnsDurableReceipt` (`SessionLogControllerReceiptTests.cs:106`) keep their outcome.
626: - Deadlock and busy (section 3.1, "Deadlock and busy outcomes"): a transient conflict inside the delegate (SQL Server 1205, PostgreSQL 40001 and 40P01, SQLite 5 and 6, `DbErrorClassifier`) reruns the delegate; at the bound the unit answers 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true`, and the plugin handles that answer as an outage (failsafe record kept, receipt `queued`). A busy store outside SerializableWrite (the dialog append and the two title writes, which keep today's single save) keeps today's 503 `persistence_error` with `retryable: true` (`McpErrorClassifier.cs:129-139` at `a8d3934b`), which the plugin also handles as an outage, and unreachable storage keeps its answer (TEST-MCP-TRIAGESTORE-007 is unchanged). The failsafe outcome of TEST-MCP-TRIAGESTORE-005, TR-MCP-TRIAGEERR-001, and FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-003 ac6 holds while their status code changes from 503 to 409 (records to update). Two develop tests change their expected outcome: `SessionLogDenseGraphTests.UpsertTurnAsyncSqlDeadlock1205DoesNotReportMissingSession` (`SessionLogDenseGraphTests.cs:100` at `a8d3934b`; its interceptor fails every reader with 1205, `:286-301`) expects the 409 `conflict` `ClassifiedErrorException` with `retryable: true` after four attempts instead of the 503 `backend_unavailable` `StorageGraphMaterializationException`, with the session not reported missing and no turn saved; `SessionLogSupersessionTests.SubmitAsyncConcurrentCompletionPreservesCompletedResponse` (`SessionLogSupersessionTests.cs:216`) expects a completion error, when one occurs, to be that 409 instead of a raw `SqliteException` 5 or 6 (`:251-254`), and its `explicitTurnWriter` row now runs the upsert in its own turn-level SerializableWrite; both keep the preserved completed turn.

1023: - Write-ahead (TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001 AC-002): under the lock the hook applies the equal-field rule, then writes the failsafe mint record (nonce, binding, root-id envelope) before the first mint call. A created, merged, or merged-terminal result, and an equal-field fail-close, clear it after the replace; an outage or a retryable answer (a transport outage, 503 `backend_unavailable`, a busy store's 503 `persistence_error`, or 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true`) keeps it for process DrainFailsafe, which opens the session before it mints; a final refusal counts as the record's first final answer (`drainAttempts` 1), so the drain mints it again under the attempt budget, each drained final answer counting one more attempt (`Resolve-MintOutcome`, section 3.5.6), and then quarantines it (process DrainFailsafe), and the Stop gate warns naming the prompt while the record is queued or quarantined. A hook killed after that write ends at the next hook, verb, or SessionStart drain with exactly one server turn for the message, delivered once (section 3.1).
1024: - First-ingress writer (hosts without a SessionStart event: classic cline, cline-v2, opencode): records a new `mcpSessionId` for the host session key only when none is recorded, in the open's replace, then opens it through `Invoke-SessionOpen` (section 3.4). From Phase C it is also the host session's Mode reader, as StartHostSession is on the other hosts: it reads the Mode with GetAgentContextStatusQuery at this first prompt and records `agentContextMode` in the same replace, `Off` when it cannot read it or does not know the value (section 3.4; section 3.1, "Mode changes").
1025: - Before the open, the hook drains its host session's failsafe when it holds drainable records (process DrainFailsafe), so an earlier prompt's mint reaches the server first.
1026: 
1027: The diagram below runs the checks that need no lock, then the open itself as one `Update-TurnState` change (nested activity OpenTurnUnderLock). The host is supported for turn logging when its P0.2 row passed and, on copilot and classic cline, the single-registration check holds; otherwise `Set-SessionUnsupported` records the failing check's reason (for example `duplicate_prompt_hook`). A system event is a task-notification, an agent-message, `agent_id`, `subagentType`, the subagent environment marker, an opencode task child session, or a host-local command that P0.2 shows produces an arrival event.
1028: 
1029: ```mermaid
1030: flowchart TD
1031:     S(["Prompt hook fires"]) --> HK{"Payload carries the host session key?"}
1032:     HK -->|no| HU(["host_session_unknown: nothing written"])
1033:     HK -->|yes| UNS{"Host supported for turn logging?"}
1034:     UNS -->|no| SU1[["Set-SessionUnsupported: the failing check"]]
1035:     SU1 --> UL(["turn_logging_unsupported: no mint"])
1036:     UNS -->|yes| SYS{"System event?"}
1037:     SYS -->|yes| SK(["system-event-skipped: no mint"])
1038:     SYS -->|no| DRN[["Process DrainFailsafe, when records are drainable"]]
1039:     DRN --> LK[["Update-TurnState: one change, never waiting"]]
1040:     LK -->|contended| CT(["turn-open-contended: diagnostic, no mint"])
1041:     LK -->|lock held| OU[["OpenTurnUnderLock"]]
1042:     OU --> REL(["State replaced, lock released: hook status"])
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ##### Nested activity: OpenTurnUnderLock (the open of OpenTurnFromPromptHook, inside one Update-TurnState change)
1046: 
1047: The equal-field check applies on copilot and classic cline: a nonce that already has a failsafe mint record or a pending turn in this host session fails the host session closed (`indistinguishable_arrival` with `causeNonce`). The write-ahead mint record carries the nonce, the binding, and the root-id envelope. The first-ingress writer applies on a host without a SessionStart event when no `mcpSessionId` is recorded for the host session. A created turn is delivered (write target, `openDelivered`, ledger entry); a merged terminal turn reports its `storedStatus` and is never the write target, in the open list, or in the ledger. The mint record follows the write-ahead rule above (`Resolve-MintOutcome`, section 3.5.6): a created, merged, or merged-terminal result and the equal-field fail-close clear it; an outage or a retryable answer keeps it for the drain; a final refusal keeps it with `drainAttempts` 1, so the drain mints it again under the attempt budget and then quarantines it (`PromptHookFinalMintRefusalRecordKeptDrainAttemptsOne`). The first-ingress writer records the new `mcpSessionId` in this replace before `Invoke-SessionOpen` runs, so an open that meets an outage keeps that identity and the drain opens the same id (`TsHostFirstIngressOpenOutageRecordedSessionIdReusedByDrainNoSecondId`).
621: 
622: - Database-only delegates: no Phase A unit reads git, files, or sources. The turn context and workspace attribution checks are path string checks against the workspace root (`SessionLogWorkspaceAttributionValidator.cs:56-105` at `a8d3934b`), so each unit runs every check inside its SerializableWrite delegate and reads nothing before it.
623: - Isolation (section 3.1, "Turn-level isolation"): the mint and the single-turn writes (upsert, patch, replace, complete, fail) read their session row only to locate the parent and write only the one turn with its children (section 3.5.2, isolation scope), so writes to different turns of one session never answer a conflict (`TurnWriteConcurrentDifferentTurnsSameSessionBothCommitNoConflictAnswer`, dense-session fixture, three providers); the session summary refresh after a single-turn write is its own short write after the turn commits, and its failure never fails the turn write. SubmitSessionLogCommand keeps its session-level Serializable transaction, as `SessionLogService.SubmitAsync` does today (`SessionLogService.cs:155-157`). The mint inserts one turn and is a single-turn write like the others (section 3.1, "Mint isolation").
624: - Retry bound: SerializableWrite runs a delegate at most four attempts, then answers 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true` and saves nothing; the attempts run within the unit's storage budget (FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-003). Only the minter states its own bound, for one cause, a collision of its random request id (six attempts, then 500 `mint_collision_exhausted`); its transient conflicts keep the default bound and the 409 `conflict` exit (section 3.1, "Retry bound").
625: - Providers: on the EF in-memory provider SerializableWrite runs the delegate once with no transaction and no retry, as develop opens its transaction only on a relational provider (`SessionLogService.cs:155`), so the 151 tests in 15 files that run the real `SessionLogService` on `UseInMemoryDatabase` keep their single run (recon `code-server.md`). A caller-owned EF or `System.Transactions` transaction is refused before any write, as develop's `SubmitAsync` refuses it (`SessionLogService.cs:119-128`); `SessionLogSupersessionTests.SubmitAsyncCallerTransactionRejectsBeforeMutation`, `SubmitAsyncAmbientTransactionRejectsBeforeMutation`, and `SubmitAsyncPendingTrackedEditRejectsWithoutDiscardingEdit` (`SessionLogSupersessionTests.cs:192,204,178` at `a8d3934b`, renamed on the analyzer branch) and `SessionLogControllerReceiptTests.SubmitAsyncOuterRollbackNeverReturnsDurableReceipt` (`SessionLogControllerReceiptTests.cs:106`) keep their outcome.
626: - Deadlock and busy (section 3.1, "Deadlock and busy outcomes"): a transient conflict inside the delegate (SQL Server 1205, PostgreSQL 40001 and 40P01, SQLite 5 and 6, `DbErrorClassifier`) reruns the delegate; at the bound the unit answers 409 `conflict` with `retryable: true`, and the plugin handles that answer as an outage (failsafe record kept, receipt `queued`). A busy store outside SerializableWrite (the dialog append and the two title writes, which keep today's single save) keeps today's 503 `persistence_error` with `retryable: true` (`McpErrorClassifier.cs:129-139` at `a8d3934b`), which the plugin also handles as an outage, and unreachable storage keeps its answer (TEST-MCP-TRIAGESTORE-007 is unchanged). The failsafe outcome of TEST-MCP-TRIAGESTORE-005, TR-MCP-TRIAGEERR-001, and FR-MCP-SESSIONLIFE-003 ac6 holds while their status code changes from 503 to 409 (records to update). Two develop tests change their expected outcome: `SessionLogDenseGraphTests.UpsertTurnAsyncSqlDeadlock1205DoesNotReportMissingSession` (`SessionLogDenseGraphTests.cs:100` at `a8d3934b`; its interceptor fails every reader with 1205, `:286-301`) expects the 409 `conflict` `ClassifiedErrorException` with `retryable: true` after four attempts instead of the 503 `backend_unavailable` `StorageGraphMaterializationException`, with the session not reported missing and no turn saved; `SessionLogSupersessionTests.SubmitAsyncConcurrentCompletionPreservesCompletedResponse` (`SessionLogSupersessionTests.cs:216`) expects a completion error, when one occurs, to be that 409 instead of a raw `SqliteException` 5 or 6 (`:251-254`), and its `explicitTurnWriter` row now runs the upsert in its own turn-level SerializableWrite; both keep the preserved completed turn.

5375: ## 8. Delivery: four execution phases and parallel domain coding
5376: 
5377: Operator directive (2026-10-11, verbatim): "I want the implementation plan to be organized into requirements as a phase, interfaces and code stubs as a phase for the entire plan, test-driven development unit tests with mocks as a single phase, and then you can begin implementation coding in a domain-driven design breakdown so that agents can be run in parallel for the coding." This section defines the delivery structure; the plan's "Execution organization" schedules it and cites this section.
5378: 
5379: ### 8.1 Phase order
5380: 
5381: ```mermaid
5382: flowchart TD
5383:     ANZ["Analyzer branch chore/netanalyzers-all merged"] --> PRE["Prerequisites (sections 8.2 and 8.4)"]
5384:     PRE --> REQ["Phase 1 Requirements: the whole catalog"]
5385:     REQ --> DES["Phase 2 Interfaces and code stubs"]
5386:     DES --> TST["Phase 3 TDD unit tests with mocks"]
5387:     TST --> IMP["Phase 4 Implementation: a coding agent per context"]
5388:     IMP --> VER["Integration, live checks, phase-wide HV, approval"]
5389: ```
5390: 
5391: The analyzer branch `chore/netanalyzers-all` merges first, before the prerequisites and Phase 1 (section 3.1, "Analyzer rules"; its work is exempt from the code freeze, section 3.1, "Code freeze exception"), so the P0.1 baseline, every Phase 2 type, and every Phase 3 test name are taken under its rules (IDE0130 namespaces, MA0048 one type per file, CA1707 test names without underscores) and at its paths: its commit `fe5879ba` moved `tests/Build.Tests` to `build/Build.Tests` (replaces the `tests/Build.Tests` path that TR-MCP-NUKE-002 names and that the evidence of TR-MCP-NUKE-002, TR-MCP-NUKE-005 to -010, and FR-MCP-PLUGININT-001 cites). Every later arrow is crossed only after that phase's gates are green with zero failures and zero skips, its hostile validation (Codex gpt-6-astra max) returns AGREE at accuracy and completeness of at least 98 with every claim PASS, and the operator approves. Section 8.2 says what each phase delivers.
5392: 
5393: Published packages: two changes of this plan reach packages that the Nuke `PackNuGet` target publishes. It packs `QBrainAI.Client`, `QBrainAI.Cqrs`, `QBrainAI.Cqrs.Mvvm`, `QBrainAI.Repl.Core`, and `QBrainAI.McpAgent` at one version, `--package-version` or the `next-version` of `GitVersion.yml` (`build/Build.PackNuGet.cs:8-9,15-43,46-74`; 1.4.40 at `a8d3934b`):
5394: 
5395: - `QBrainAI.Client` grows in Phase 2: the new DTOs (`QBrainAi.Client.Models.SessionLog`, `QBrainAi.Client.Models.AgentContext`), `ClassifiedErrorException` and `ErrorCodes` (`QBrainAi.Client.Errors`), `PageResult<TItem>` (`QBrainAi.Client.Paging`), and `ScoreLexeme` with `ScoreLexemeJsonConverter` (`QBrainAi.Client.Scoring`) become public API beside the existing `McpClientException` family (`src/QBrainAi.Client/McpClientExceptions.cs:15-27`), which stays the typed error the client raises to its callers. Every change is an addition, so its version effect is a minor version.
5396: - `QBrainAI.Cqrs` changes in Phase 4 (SharedComponents): `IDispatcher` becomes the scoped facade of section 3.5.1 ("Dispatch scope") in place of today's singleton registration (`src/QBrainAi.Cqrs/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:22-27`). Every public signature stays, but a consumer that resolves `IDispatcher` from the root provider or injects it into a singleton fails under DI scope validation (inference), so its version effect is a major version under semantic versioning.
5397: 
5398: The first release after Phase 4 publishes both changes. Every `QBrainAI.*` package shares the one version, and FR-MCP-QBRAIN-004 ends the 1.x configuration aliases at 2.0, so the operator sets that release's version at the release (Octopus), and its release notes name both changes.
5399: 
5400: ### 8.2 What each phase delivers
5401: 
5402: - Prerequisites, after the analyzer branch has merged: every pre-existing failure fixed under its own TODO (P0.1, including the Windows findings), the REPL `generateDocument` validator fix, the Nuke targets every later gate runs through (`Test --test-projects --test-filter`, which also reaches the integration and validation projects of G3, section 8.4; `TestPluginCore`; `TestAgentPlugins`), the port of every bats case to Pester (P0.1b; Pester is the only plugin test runner, operator, 2026-10-11: "You should be designing all scripts and script tools around PowerShell and only PowerShell."), `build/Build.Tests` removed from `MigrationIntegrationTests` (P0.1c, TR-MCP-NUKE-014; the analyzer branch moved the project and still lists it there, `build/Build.TestDependencies.cs:73` on `chore/netanalyzers-all`), BUG-BUILD-005 fixed before the first G5 run, and BUG-BUILD-008 landed at its plugin version 1.119.0 before this plan's sync (both in section 8.4).
5403: - Phase 1, requirements (the plan's P0 steps 1-9): the whole catalog of Phases A, B, and C created in the requirement store from this architecture and the plan's requirement catalog, the use cases, the feature matrix rows, and the phase and domain TODOs (`REQ-MERGEDPLAN-001`, `DESIGN-MERGEDPLAN-001`, `TEST-MERGEDPLAN-001`, one `IMPL-<CONTEXT>-001` per bounded context, `VERIFY-MERGEDPLAN-001`).
5404: - Phase 2, interfaces and code stubs: every command and query record with a handler stub, every policy and seam interface with a stub, every section 3.5 component with its Phase 2 seam and a stub (the two CQRS behaviors registered as pass-through stubs that call the next handler, and `IDispatcher` kept at today's registration until SharedComponents changes it, so existing behavior stays live), every new entity class and its `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` as compiling, unregistered classes (no `DbSet`, no registration in `McpDbContext`, and no new property on an existing entity, because `McpDbContext.cs:301-308` ignores the pending-model-changes warning, so a registered model change without its migration would make queries select columns the database lacks and regress the existing tests that call `Migrate()`; the registered model change, the three migrations, and the S3 backfill belong to the Phase 4 context StorageSchema), every DTO and client mirror with JSON context registration, every controller route, MCP tool, client method, and REPL method (they only dispatch, and each controller route and MCP tool maps its unit's typed failures to the bodies of the unit's error list, section 8.3), every new plugin function and tool signature in `plugins/core/lib-ps`, the options classes and `appsettings.yaml` sections, DI, and the golden contract files. Stubs return neutral values and never throw, so Phase 3 tests fail on assertions. Existing behavior stays live: the handlers of the units that wrap today's routes are delegating handlers that call today's `ISessionLogService` members unchanged, so every existing route, tool, REPL method, and plugin path behaves as today and the existing suites stay green; only the new members and new units are stubs, reached by no existing path, and each Phase 4 context switches its delegating handlers to the new members when its Phase 3 tests go green. No plugin repo changes before Phase 4: the TypeScript hosts keep their current adapters and Jest suites until HostPluginAdoption replaces both in one change after the sync (A9).
5405: - Phase 3, unit tests with mocks: every unit test the catalog names, written from the acceptance criteria, recorded RED against the stubs, then green against mocks with the oracle and mutant pattern and a recorded negative check each. A Phase 2 change that completes behavior rather than stubbing it (the `agent_context` federation registration, FR-MCP-103-AC006) records its case red in Phase 2, before the change, and Phase 3 keeps it green (section 3.1, Test placement). Each section 3.5 component gets its one test class (for example `SerializableWriteTests`); a unit's tests mock the component's Phase 2 seam and never test the component's own branches again.
5406: - Phase 4, implementation: each bounded context replaces its stubs with the real implementation until its Phase 3 tests pass unchanged, adds its integration tests, and runs its gates; then the contexts merge in the rollout order and the integration gates, live checks, and phase-wide HV run.
5407: 
5408: ### 8.3 Bounded contexts (Phase 4 work packages)
5409: 
5410: The diagram draws merge order only: a context starts when every context with an arrow into it has merged. StorageSchema (the registered model change, the migrations for three providers, the S3 backfill) runs first and alone; SharedComponents (sections 3.5.1 and 3.5.2, with the `QBrainAi.Cqrs` dispatch scope) runs second and alone; then the six server contexts run in parallel. PluginCorePowerShell and BuildTooling call no C# component, so they run in parallel from the start of Phase 4; HostPluginAdoption follows both, and Documentation runs last. Calls between contexts go through the callee's Phase 2 seam and never wait for the callee to merge, so they draw no arrow; they are listed after the context bullets below.
5411: 
5412: ```mermaid
5413: flowchart LR
5414:     SS["StorageSchema: first, alone"] --> SC["SharedComponents: second, alone"]
5415:     subgraph Server["Server contexts, in parallel"]
5416:         STL["SessionTurnLogging"]
5417:         TR["TurnReviews"]

5555: ### 8.4 Gates
5556: 
5557: - G1 targeted tests through `./build.ps1 Test --test-projects --test-filter`, G2 the unit gate (`./build.ps1 Test`), G3 integration suites (next bullet), G4 the PowerShell plugin core through `./build.ps1 TestPluginCore`, G5 config and traceability (`./build.ps1 ValidateConfig`, `./build.ps1 ValidateTraceability`), G6 the plugin suites through `./build.ps1 TestAgentPlugins`: Pester in the six PowerShell-host repos (selected with `--plugins`) for every exit before HostPluginAdoption, because the TypeScript hosts keep their Jest suites until HostPluginAdoption replaces them, and Pester in all nine repos from HostPluginAdoption on, including the phase-wide Phase 4 exit. Named prerequisite (P0.1a, TR-MCP-NUKE-011): no Nuke target runs those four projects today, because `Test` leaves out every `*.IntegrationTests` and `*.Validation` project and filters out `Category=Integration`, the trait the integration projects' classes carry (`build/Build.Test.cs:16-24,50`, `build/Build.TestDependencies.cs:60-61`), and `MigrationIntegrationTests` runs only `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Tests` and Build.Tests (`build/Build.TestDependencies.cs:70-74`). 5578: - Merge and deploy order: StorageSchema, SharedComponents, SessionTurnLogging, TurnReviews without the CompletionGate enforcement change set, ContextPackages, ResponsesAndTrust, ContextGraph, ReplAndAgents; deploy the server (agent context Mode `Off`: the plugins stay stateful, every gated agent-context command answers 409 `agent_context_disabled`, and the read-only agent-context queries answer); merge PluginCorePowerShell, BuildTooling; sync all nine plugins once at one explicit version (`./build.ps1 SyncAgentPlugins --agent-plugin-parent /home/sharpninja/github --plugin-version 1.120.0`, after BUG-BUILD-008 has landed at 1.119.0, section 8.4; it carries the Phase A, B, and C plugin work together; the installed-equals-synced step, which the sync's own refresh of the installed caches of that version begins, and the operator's codex hook trust follow, and a same-version re-sync, which refreshes content and never bumps the version, runs only when a later Phase 4 fix changes `plugins/core/lib-ps`); merge HostPluginAdoption, whose exit runs `./build.ps1 ValidatePluginPowerShellOnly --agent-plugin-parent /home/sharpninja/github` over the tracked trees of all nine repos (section 8.4); then `MAINT-LIBSHRETIRE-001`, and, once Codex ACKs the 2026-10-12 PowerShell-only CONTRACT entry or the operator resolves it, `MAINT-LIBNODERETIRE-001`; merge and deploy the CompletionGate enforcement change set, whose deploy receipt lists the workspace's turns in progress at that moment (QuerySessionLogsQuery, status `in_progress`): the gate refuses their completion until each carries the items it names, the Stop gate remedy names them, and nothing is backfilled (section 3.1, Turns open at the CompletionGate deploy); Documentation; then the integration checks.
5579: - Migrations: StorageSchema's three migrations per provider run Up, Down, and Up again on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server in G3 (`./build.ps1 MigrationIntegrationTests`), with the schema and the data equal after the second Up (`MigrationsUpDownUpThreeProvidersSchemaAndDataEqual`); a migration rolls back only through that tested Down.
5580: - Binary-only rollback (`UpdateService` to the prior build while the schema stays at the new migrations): the new required review status columns carry the database default `Unstarted`, and `RequestClass` the database default `Unclassified`, so a turn the prior binary inserts during the rollback reads as its ReviewDefaults after the roll-forward, which runs no second backfill (`RollbackPriorBinaryInsertsTurnRollForwardReadsDefaults`); the Phase C tables are new, and the prior binary never writes them.
5581: - Readable keys across workspaces: every readable key is per workspace (section 6.3, a composite key with `WorkspaceId`), so two workspaces that hold the same legacy request id get the same key string on two rows, with no collision and no retry exhaustion, before and after the rollout (`ReadableKeyAllocatorSameParentIdTwoWorkspacesSameKeyNoCollisionNoExhaustion`).
5582: - On the shared servers, Mode `Pilot` only on the operator's instruction (the agent-context live check runs on its own instance, section 8.6). A change away from `Off` takes effect at each host session's next start, and only on hosts whose prompt hook can refuse a prompt (P0.2 probe (j)); any other host, and a host that runs the prompt anyway after a hook timeout, crash, or `plugin_core_unavailable`, runs `Pilot` and `Stateless` as `Off` with the limitation in its feature-matrix row. The pilot report goes to the operator: `Pilot` yields stateful responses with packages built and graded, a period in `Stateless` on hosts with history exclusion yields stateless responses, and the report compares them by `invocationMode` and also counts `Overflow` packages, refused prompts, and requests with a package and no response. `Stateless` as a default is a later operator decision taken from that report.
5583: - Server deploys run through the Nuke `UpdateService` target with operator approval; releases use Octopus only. Rollback: Mode `Off` stops agent-context behavior without a deploy, and `Off` means stateful continuation: a running host session whose plugin cached `Pilot` or `Stateless` gets 409 `agent_context_disabled` at its next build or submission, caches `Off`, and continues statefully (no refusal, no `canceled` close; every other build error still fails the invocation), and a plugin that cannot read the Mode at host session start, including a read that misses the SessionStart hook bound, assumes `Off`. The stored packages, responses, grades, relationships, HV requests, and the pilot report stay readable in `Off` for audit. Schema rollback follows the migrations bullet above.
5584: 
5585: ### 8.6 End-to-end verification
5586: 
5587: - Turn logging and reviews: the live checks of the plan's "End-to-end verification" section.
5588: - Agent context, on LAB-OMARCHY and PAYTON-LEGION2, each on a separate server instance started for the check with its own `--instance`, Mode `Pilot`, and explicit `ProfileSources` and `RuleSources`, never on a shared server (so no other live agent session is subject to prompt refusal, and the profile never resolves in a service account's home): a delivered request builds one package with the request's root ids (on claude-code and claude-cowork the prompt hook takes the bridge-minted `requestId` after applying pending transcript records); replay reports `identical: true`; an over-budget fixture prompt is refused with `agent_context_budget_exceeded` shown to the operator, no answer is produced, and the request's turn is closed `canceled` with that reason and leaves the Stop ledger once the server confirms the close, and a retried build with the same idempotency key returns the same 422 with the stored diagnostics; the model submits its response with the `agent_context_submit_response` tool before closing the turn, and the response passes the deterministic grade; an HV request covering its turn is created, the HV agent records a passing model grade with verified receipts, and the response becomes `Trusted`; a later package includes it as a prior response; committing a change to a file it depends on makes it `Stale` (an uncommitted edit does not, because staleness reads files at the workspace HEAD commit); with GraphRAG disabled retrieval reports `graphrag_disabled` and answers from the relational path; with GraphRAG enabled the trusted response is projected and a rejected one removed; the pilot report lists these requests by `invocationMode` (all `Stateful` under `Pilot`) and counts the `Overflow` package and the refused prompt; switching the instance to Mode `Off` while a host session runs makes its next build answer 409 `agent_context_disabled`, after which the host session continues statefully with no refusal and no `canceled` close, and the read-only queries, the pilot report among them, still answer.

5578: - Merge and deploy order: StorageSchema, SharedComponents, SessionTurnLogging, TurnReviews without the CompletionGate enforcement change set, ContextPackages, ResponsesAndTrust, ContextGraph, ReplAndAgents; deploy the server (agent context Mode `Off`: the plugins stay stateful, every gated agent-context command answers 409 `agent_context_disabled`, and the read-only agent-context queries answer); merge PluginCorePowerShell, BuildTooling; sync all nine plugins once at one explicit version (`./build.ps1 SyncAgentPlugins --agent-plugin-parent /home/sharpninja/github --plugin-version 1.120.0`, after BUG-BUILD-008 has landed at 1.119.0, section 8.4; it carries the Phase A, B, and C plugin work together; the installed-equals-synced step, which the sync's own refresh of the installed caches of that version begins, and the operator's codex hook trust follow, and a same-version re-sync, which refreshes content and never bumps the version, runs only when a later Phase 4 fix changes `plugins/core/lib-ps`); merge HostPluginAdoption, whose exit runs `./build.ps1 ValidatePluginPowerShellOnly --agent-plugin-parent /home/sharpninja/github` over the tracked trees of all nine repos (section 8.4); then `MAINT-LIBSHRETIRE-001`, and, once Codex ACKs the 2026-10-12 PowerShell-only CONTRACT entry or the operator resolves it, `MAINT-LIBNODERETIRE-001`; merge and deploy the CompletionGate enforcement change set, whose deploy receipt lists the workspace's turns in progress at that moment (QuerySessionLogsQuery, status `in_progress`): the gate refuses their completion until each carries the items it names, the Stop gate remedy names them, and nothing is backfilled (section 3.1, Turns open at the CompletionGate deploy); Documentation; then the integration checks.
5579: - Migrations: StorageSchema's three migrations per provider run Up, Down, and Up again on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server in G3 (`./build.ps1 MigrationIntegrationTests`), with the schema and the data equal after the second Up (`MigrationsUpDownUpThreeProvidersSchemaAndDataEqual`); a migration rolls back only through that tested Down.
5580: - Binary-only rollback (`UpdateService` to the prior build while the schema stays at the new migrations): the new required review status columns carry the database default `Unstarted`, and `RequestClass` the database default `Unclassified`, so a turn the prior binary inserts during the rollback reads as its ReviewDefaults after the roll-forward, which runs no second backfill (`RollbackPriorBinaryInsertsTurnRollForwardReadsDefaults`); the Phase C tables are new, and the prior binary never writes them.
5581: - Readable keys across workspaces: every readable key is per workspace (section 6.3, a composite key with `WorkspaceId`), so two workspaces that hold the same legacy request id get the same key string on two rows, with no collision and no retry exhaustion, before and after the rollout (`ReadableKeyAllocatorSameParentIdTwoWorkspacesSameKeyNoCollisionNoExhaustion`).
5582: - On the shared servers, Mode `Pilot` only on the operator's instruction (the agent-context live check runs on its own instance, section 8.6). A change away from `Off` takes effect at each host session's next start, and only on hosts whose prompt hook can refuse a prompt (P0.2 probe (j)); any other host, and a host that runs the prompt anyway after a hook timeout, crash, or `plugin_core_unavailable`, runs `Pilot` and `Stateless` as `Off` with the limitation in its feature-matrix row. The pilot report goes to the operator: `Pilot` yields stateful responses with packages built and graded, a period in `Stateless` on hosts with history exclusion yields stateless responses, and the report compares them by `invocationMode` and also counts `Overflow` packages, refused prompts, and requests with a package and no response. `Stateless` as a default is a later operator decision taken from that report.
5583: - Server deploys run through the Nuke `UpdateService` target with operator approval; releases use Octopus only. Rollback: Mode `Off` stops agent-context behavior without a deploy, and `Off` means stateful continuation: a running host session whose plugin cached `Pilot` or `Stateless` gets 409 `agent_context_disabled` at its next build or submission, caches `Off`, and continues statefully (no refusal, no `canceled` close; every other build error still fails the invocation), and a plugin that cannot read the Mode at host session start, including a read that misses the SessionStart hook bound, assumes `Off`. The stored packages, responses, grades, relationships, HV requests, and the pilot report stay readable in `Off` for audit. Schema rollback follows the migrations bullet above.
